title.zh: 卷三百九十 列傳第一百四十九 李衡 王自中 家愿 張綱 張大經 蔡洸 莫濛 周淙 劉章 沈作賓
title.en: Volume 390 Biographies 149: Li Heng, Wang Zizhong, Jia Yuan, Zhang Gang, Zhang Dajing, Cai Guang, Mo Meng, Zhou Cong, Liu Zhang, Shen Zuobin
title.raw: 卷三百九十 列傳第一百四十九 李衡 王自中 家愿 張綱 張大經 蔡洸 莫濛 周淙 劉章 沈作賓 Volume 390 Biographies 149: Li Heng, Wang Zizhong, Jia Yuan, Zhang Gang, Zhang Dajing, Cai Guang, Mo Meng, Zhou Cong, Liu Zhang, Shen Zuobin

sentences.zh: 李衡王自中家愿张纲张大经蔡洸莫濛周淙刘章沈作宾

translations.literal: Li Heng, Wang Zizhong, Jia Yuan, Zhang Gang, Zhang Dajing, Cai Guang, Mo Meng, Zhou Cong, Liu Zhang, and Shen Zuobin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng, Wang Zizhong, Jia Yuan, Zhang Gang, Zhang Dajing, Cai Guang, Mo Meng, Zhou Cong, Liu Zhang, and Shen Zuobin.

sentences.zh: 李衡，字彦平，江都人。

translations.literal: Li Heng, style name Yanping, was a man of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng, courtesy name Yanping, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 高祖昭素仕至侍御史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhaosu served in office up to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhaosu rose in office to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 衡幼善博诵，为文操笔立就。

translations.literal: From youth Heng was skilled at broad recitation; when he took up the brush to write, completion came at once.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, Heng excelled at wide reading and memorization, and when he wrote, his compositions were finished the moment he picked up the brush.

sentences.zh: 登进士第，授 吴江主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Registrar of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed registrar of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 有部使者怙势作威，侵刻下民，衡不忍以敲扑迎合，投劾于府，拂衣而归。

translations.literal: There was a departmental envoy who relied on power to display authority and oppressed the people below; Heng could not bear to win favor through beating and flogging, submitted an impeachment to the prefecture, shook out his robes, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A departmental envoy relied on his rank to bully others and grind down the common people. Heng refused to win favor through beatings and floggings, filed an impeachment with the prefectural office, and walked away from his post.

sentences.zh: 后知溧阳县，专以诚意化民，民莫不敬。

translations.literal: Later he governed Liyang County, devoting himself solely to transforming the people through sincere intent, and none of the people failed to revere him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Liyang County, he devoted himself to governing through sincerity alone, and the people all held him in respect.

sentences.zh: 夏秋二税，以期日榜县门，乡无府吏 迹，而输送先他邑办。

translations.literal: For the summer and autumn two taxes, he posted the due dates at the county gate; in the countryside there were no traces of prefectural clerks, yet delivery was completed before other counties.
translations.idiomatic: For the summer and autumn tax levies, he posted the due dates at the county gate. No prefectural clerks appeared in the villages, yet his county finished its deliveries ahead of every other jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 因任历四年，狱户未尝系一重囚。

translations.literal: Throughout his four years in office, the prison cells never once held a serious offender.
translations.idiomatic: During his four-year tenure, not a single serious prisoner ever occupied the jail.

sentences.zh: 隆兴二年，金犯淮堧，人相惊曰：“寇深矣！

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing, when the Jin invaded the Huai frontier, people cried out to one another in alarm, saying, "The invaders have come deep!
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longxing, when the Jin attacked the Huai frontier, people cried out to one another in alarm: "The enemy is upon us!

sentences.zh: ”官沿江者多送其孥，衡独自浙右移家入县，民 心大安。

translations.literal: " Many officials along the river sent away their wives and children; Heng alone moved his household from west of Zhejiang into the county, and the people's hearts were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: " Many officials along the Yangzi sent their families away. Heng alone moved his household from Zhejiang into the county, and the people were greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 盗猬起旁境，而溧阳靖晏自如。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed up in neighboring jurisdictions, yet Liyang remained peaceful and calm as before.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits erupted everywhere in neighboring counties, yet Liyang remained as peaceful and orderly as ever.

sentences.zh: 帅汪澈、转运使韩元吉等列上治状，诏进一秩，寻召入为监察御史。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner Wang Che, transport commissioner Han Yuanji, and others submitted memorials on his governance; an edict advanced his rank by one step, and soon he was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wang Che, Transport Commissioner Han Yuanji, and others memorialized the throne praising his administration. The court promoted him one rank and soon summoned him to serve as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 历司封郎中、枢密院检详，出知温、婺、台三州，惟婺 尝莅其治。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director in the Bureau of Appointments and Reviewer at the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was sent out to govern Wen, Wu, and Tai Prefectures, but only Wu did he actually administer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Bureau of Appointments and as reviewer at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then was sent out to govern Wenzhou, Wuzhou, and Taizhou—though in fact he governed only Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 加直秘阁，而衡引年乞身，恳恳不休，上累却其奏，除秘阁修撰致仕。

translations.literal: He was given Direct Associate of the Secretariat Archive, but Heng cited his age and petitioned to retire, pleading earnestly without cease; the emperor repeatedly rejected his memorials and appointed him Compiler of the Secretariat Archive with permission to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to direct associate of the Secretariat Archive, but Heng cited his age and repeatedly petitioned to retire. The emperor rejected his requests several times before finally appointing him compiler of the Secretariat Archive and granting him retirement.

sentences.zh: 上思其仆忠，旋召落致仕，除侍御史，以老固辞，不获命。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of his plain loyalty, soon recalled him and removed his retirement status, appointing him Attending Censor; citing age, he firmly declined but could not refuse the order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering his simple-hearted loyalty, soon recalled him from retirement and appointed him attending censor. Heng firmly declined on account of his age, but the appointment could not be refused.

sentences.zh: 差同知贡举。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Associate Commissioner for the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate commissioner for the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 会外戚张 说以节度使掌兵柄，衡力疏其事，谓“不当以母后肺腑为人择官”，廷争移时。

translations.literal: It happened that the empress's kinsman Zhang Shuo held military authority as military commissioner; Heng vigorously memorialized against this, saying, "One ought not choose officials for others merely because they are close kin to the empress dowager," and debated at court for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empress's kinsman Zhang Shuo held military power as a military commissioner. Heng vigorously memorialized against the appointment, declaring that officials ought not be chosen merely because they were close kin to the empress dowager, and debated the matter at court at length.

sentences.zh: 改除起居郎，衡曰：“与其进而负于君，孰若退而合于道。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Movements. Heng said, "Better to withdraw in accordance with the Way than to advance and fail the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as recorder of the emperor's movements. Heng said, "Better to withdraw in accordance with the Way than to advance and betray the sovereign.

sentences.zh: ”章五上，请老愈力，上 知不可夺，仍以秘撰致仕。

translations.literal: " He submitted five memorials and pressed his request for retirement with growing force; the emperor knew he could not be dissuaded and again granted him retirement as Compiler of the Secretariat Archive.
translations.idiomatic: " He submitted five memorials, pressing his request for retirement with ever greater force. The emperor knew he could not be dissuaded and again granted him retirement as compiler of the Secretariat Archive.

sentences.zh: 时给事中莫济不书敕，翰林周必大不草制，右正言王希吕亦与衡相继论奏，同时去国，士为《四贤诗》以纪之。

translations.literal: At the time Supervising Secretary Mo Ji refused to inscribe the edicts, Hanlin Academician Zhou Bidà refused to draft the proclamations, and Right Remonstrating Official Wang Xilü also joined Heng in successive memorials and remonstrances; they left office at the same time, and scholars composed Four Worthies Poems to commemorate them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Supervising Secretary Mo Ji refused to inscribe the edicts, Hanlin Academician Zhou Bidà refused to draft the proclamations, and Right Remonstrating Official Wang Xilü joined Heng in a succession of memorials and remonstrances. They all left office together, and scholars composed Four Worthies Poems in their honor.

sentences.zh: 衡后定居昆山，结茅别 墅，杖屦徜徉，左右惟二苍头，聚书逾万卷，号曰“乐庵”，卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: Heng later settled permanently in Kunshan, built a thatched villa, and wandered with staff and sandals; he was attended by only two household servants, amassed more than ten thousand volumes of books, and called his retreat Joy Hermitage. He died at seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Heng later settled permanently in Kunshan, where he built a thatched retreat and wandered at leisure with staff and sandals. Only two household servants attended him, and he amassed more than ten thousand volumes of books in a library he called Joy Hermitage. He died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 衡自宣和间入辟雍，同舍有赵孝孙者，洛人也，其父实师程颐，家学有 源，劝衡读《论语》曰：“学非记诵辞章之谓，所以学圣贤也，不可有丝毫伪实处，方可以言学。

translations.literal: From the Xuanhe era Heng entered the Imperial Academy; among his roommates was one Zhao Xiaosun, a man of Luoyang whose father had in fact studied under Cheng Yi—his family learning had a true source. He urged Heng to read the Analects, saying, "Learning is not what is meant by memorization and literary composition; it is learning from the sages and worthies. Unless there is not the slightest falsity in one's conduct, one cannot speak of learning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xuanhe era onward, Heng studied at the Imperial Academy. Among his roommates was Zhao Xiaosun of Luoyang, whose father had studied under Cheng Yi—his family learning had a genuine lineage. He urged Heng to read the Analects, saying, "Learning is not mere memorization and literary polish; it is learning from the sages. Unless there is not the slightest falsity in one's conduct, one cannot speak of learning at all.

sentences.zh: ”衡心佩其训，虽博通群书而以《论语》为根本。

translations.literal: " Heng took his teaching to heart; though broadly learned in many books, he took the Analects as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: " Heng took this teaching to heart. Though widely read in many books, he took the Analects as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 临没，沐浴冠 栉，翛然而逝。

translations.literal: At the approach of death he bathed, put on his cap, and combed his hair, then passed away with serene ease.
translations.idiomatic: At the end, he bathed, dressed his hair, and put on his cap, then passed away with serene composure.

sentences.zh: 周必大闻之曰：“世谓潜心释氏，乃能达死生，衡非逃儒入释者，而临终超然如此，殆几孔门所谓闻道者欤。

translations.literal: When Zhou Bidà heard of it he said, "The world says only those who devote themselves to Buddhism can comprehend life and death. Heng was no Confucian who fled into Buddhism, yet at his end he was so transcendent—perhaps he nearly attained what the Confucian school calls one who has heard the Way.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Bidà heard of it, he said, "People say that only those who devote themselves to Buddhism can transcend life and death. Heng was no Confucian who fled into Buddhism, yet at his end he was so serene—perhaps he nearly attained what the Confucian school calls one who has heard the Way.

sentences.zh: 王自中

translations.literal: Wang Zizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 王自中，字道甫，温州平阳人。

translations.literal: Wang Zizhong, style name Daofu, was a man of Pingyang in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhong, courtesy name Daofu, was a native of Pingyang in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 少负奇气，自立崖岸，繇是忤世。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed unusual spirit and stood apart on his own cliff-edge; thus he offended the world.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he possessed an uncommon spirit and held himself apart on a lofty standard, and so he ran afoul of the world.

sentences.zh: 乾道四年，议遣归正人，自中伏丽正门争论，且言：“今内空无贤，外空无兵，当搜罗豪俊，广募忠力，以图中原。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiandao, when the court debated sending back the returned-righteous people, Zizhong prostrated himself at the Lizheng Gate to argue, saying, "Today within we lack worthy men, without we lack troops—we ought to gather bold talents and widely recruit loyal strength to recover the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiandao, when the court debated repatriating Jin defectors, Zizhong prostrated himself at the Lizheng Gate to remonstrate, saying, "Within the realm we lack worthy men; beyond it we lack troops. We ought to gather bold talents and widely recruit loyal strength to recover the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: ”坐斥徽州，放还。

translations.literal: " He was demoted and sent to Qizhou, then released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: " For this he was demoted and sent to Qizhou, then released to return home.

sentences.zh: 淳熙中，登进士第，主舒州怀宁簿。

translations.literal: During the Chunxi era he passed the jinshi examination and served as Registrar of Huaining in Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunxi era he passed the jinshi examination and served as registrar of Huaining in Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 严州分水令。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Fenshui in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Fenshui in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 枢密使王蔺荐，召对，帝壮其言，将改秩为籍田令，又俾举所知，且响用矣，以谏疏罢。

translations.literal: When Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Lin recommended him, he was summoned for an audience; the emperor was impressed by his words and was about to promote him to Director of the Sacrificial Fields and also have him recommend men he knew—the appointment was nearly made—when he was dismissed on account of a remonstrance memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Lin recommended him, he was summoned for an audience. The emperor was impressed by his words and was about to promote him to director of the sacrificial fields and have him recommend men he knew—the appointment was nearly at hand—when he was dismissed because of a remonstrance memorial.

sentences.zh: 自中本韩彦古客，王蔺既荐之，上大喜。

translations.literal: Zizhong had originally been a client of Han Yangu; once Wang Lin recommended him, the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhong had originally been a client of Han Yangu. Once Wang Lin recommended him, the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 韩彦直、彦质辈恐其为彦古报 仇，力请交结于自中；

translations.literal: Han Yanzhi, Yanzhi's faction, and others feared he would avenge Han Yangu and strongly urged Zizhong to seek their alliance;
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi, Yanzhi, and their faction feared he would avenge Han Yangu and strongly urged Zizhong to seek their alliance;

sentences.zh: 而密达意近习，谓“自中受彦古赂，伏阙上书荐彦古为相。

translations.literal: while secretly conveying word to court favorites that "Zizhong accepted bribes from Han Yangu and prostrated himself at the palace gate to memorialize recommending Han Yangu as chief councilor."
translations.idiomatic: while secretly telling court favorites that Zizhong had accepted bribes from Han Yangu and prostrated himself at the palace gate to recommend Han Yangu as chief councilor.

sentences.zh: ”上遣人物色其事，中书舍人王信恒惧自中入台将不利于王淮，知彦直辈谮已行， 亟请对，探上意；

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to investigate the matter; Drafting Middle Secretary Wang Xin constantly feared that if Zizhong entered the Censorate it would harm Wang Huai. Knowing the Han faction's slander had already taken hold, he urgently requested an audience and probed the emperor's intent;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to investigate. Drafting Middle Secretary Wang Xin constantly feared that if Zizhong entered the Censorate it would harm Wang Huai. Learning that the Han faction's slander had already taken hold, he urgently requested an audience and probed the emperor's intent;

sentences.zh: 退即走白右正言蒋继周。

translations.literal: upon withdrawing he immediately ran to inform Right Remonstrating Official Jiang Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving the audience he immediately ran to inform Right Remonstrating Official Jiang Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 继周方敢劾奏，读至“受赂伏阙”处，上曰：“卿可谓中其膏肓。

translations.literal: Only then did Jizhou dare to impeach; when he read the passage about "accepting bribes and prostrating at the palace gate," the emperor said, "Your memorial truly strikes at his vital point."
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jizhou dare to impeach. When he read the passage about "accepting bribes and prostrating at the palace gate," the emperor said, "Your memorial truly strikes at his vital point."

sentences.zh: ”继周奏：“臣非不知孤踪忤王蔺，但不敢旷职。

translations.literal: Jizhou submitted, "Your subject knows he stands alone against Wang Lin, but he dares not neglect his duty."
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou submitted, "Your subject knows he stands alone against Wang Lin, but he dares not neglect his duty."

sentences.zh: ”盖 欲并中蔺以媚淮，上但喜继周善论事，不知曲折如此。

translations.literal: In essence he wished also to hit Lin while flattering Huai; the emperor merely applauded Jizhou's eloquence, unaware of all these twists.
translations.idiomatic: In essence he wished also to strike at Lin while flattering Huai. The emperor merely applauded Jizhou's eloquence, unaware of all these twists.

sentences.zh: 通判郢州，道除知光化军，改信州，丁内艰，服阕，还朝。

translations.literal: Supervising Prefect of Ezhou; en route he was appointed Military Commissioner of Guanghua; transferred to Xinzhou; upon mourning for his mother, after the mourning period he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervising prefect of Ezhou; en route he was appointed military commissioner of Guanghua, then transferred to Xinzhou. After completing mourning for his mother, he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，迎谓曰：“朕得卿名于寿皇，留为郎可乎？

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he greeted him and said, "I learned your name from Emperor Shouhuang—will you stay on as a court officer?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he greeted him and said, "I learned your name from Emperor Shouhuang—will you stay on as a court officer?"

sentences.zh: ”言者不置。

translations.literal: Critics did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Critics objected.

sentences.zh: 主管冲佑观，起知邵州、兴化军，命下而自中已病，庆元五年八月，卒，年六十。

translations.literal: Director of the Chongyou Abbey; later appointed to govern Shaozhou and Xinghua Circuit—but the order came after Zizhong was already ill. In the eighth month of the fifth year of Qingyuan he died at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the Chongyou Abbey, then appointed to govern Shaozhou and Xinghua Circuit—but the order arrived after Zizhong was already ill. In the eighth month of the fifth year of Qingyuan he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 家愿，字处厚，眉山人。

translations.literal: Jia Yuan, style name Chuhou, was a man of Meishan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yuan, courtesy name Chuhou, was a native of Meishan.

sentences.zh: 父勤国，庆历、嘉祐间与从兄安国、定国同从刘巨游，与苏轼兄弟为同门友。

translations.literal: His father Qinguo, between the Qingli and Jiayou eras, studied together with his older cousins Anguo and Dingguo under Liu Ju, and were fellow students with the Su brothers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinguo, during the Qingli and Jiayou eras, studied with his older cousins Anguo and Dingguo under Liu Ju and were fellow students with the Su brothers.

sentences.zh: 王安石久废《春秋》学，勤国愤之，著《春秋新义》。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi had long neglected Spring and Autumn studies; Qinguo was indignant and wrote New Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had long neglected the study of the Spring and Autumn Annals; Qinguo was indignant and wrote New Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 熙宁、元丰诸人纷更，而元祐诸贤矫枉过正，勤国忧之，为筑室，作《室喻》，二苏读之敬叹。

translations.literal: During the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms many changes were made rashly; when the Yuanyou worthies overcorrected, Qinguo was troubled, built a studio, and wrote Studio Allegory, which the two Sus read with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining and Yuanfeng reforms many changes were made rashly; when the Yuanyou worthies overcorrected, Qinguo was troubled, built a studio, and wrote Studio Allegory, which the two Sus read with admiration.

sentences.zh: 愿弱冠游京师，以广文馆进士登第，时绍圣元年也。

translations.literal: At twenty Yuan traveled to the capital, passed through the Broad Culture Hall examination, and received his degree in the first year of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Yuan traveled to the capital, passed the Broad Culture Hall examination, and received his degree in the first year of Shaosheng.

sentences.zh: 廷策进士，中书侍郎李清臣拟进策问，力诋元祐之政，愿答策惟以守九年之所已行者为言。

translations.literal: At the palace examination, Vice Director Li Qingchen proposed the policy question and strongly attacked Yuanyou policies; Yuan answered only by advocating adherence to what had been implemented over the past nine years.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination, Vice Director Li Qingchen drafted the policy question and fiercely attacked Yuanyou policies. Yuan answered only by advocating adherence to what had already been implemented over the past nine years.

sentences.zh: 时门下侍郎苏辙尝 上疏辨策问，举汉武帝事，触上怒待罪，愿未及知也，因见辙，诵所对，惊喜曰：“故人子道同志合，犹若是也。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Su Zhe had memorialized disputing the policy question, citing Emperor Wu of Han, provoking imperial anger and awaiting punishment; Yuan did not yet know. Upon meeting Zhe he recited his answer, and Zhe said in delight, "The son of an old friend—same path, same purpose—still thus!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Director Su Zhe had memorialized disputing the policy question, citing Emperor Wu of Han, provoking the emperor's anger and leaving him awaiting punishment. Yuan did not yet know. When he met Zhe he recited his answer, and Zhe said in delight, "The son of an old friend—same path, same purpose—still thus!"

sentences.zh: ”杨畏覆考，专主熙宁、元丰，取毕渐为第一，愿 遂居下第。

translations.literal: Yang Wei reviewed the examination, exclusively favoring Xining and Yuanfeng policies, ranked Bi Jian first, and Yuan fell to the lowest rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei reviewed the examination, exclusively favoring Xining and Yuanfeng policies, ranked Bi Jian first, and Yuan fell to the lowest rank.

sentences.zh: 辙寻出守汝，而国论大变矣。

translations.literal: Zhe soon went out to govern Ru Prefecture, and the political tide shifted greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe soon went out to govern Ru Prefecture, and the political tide shifted greatly.

sentences.zh: 元符三年，以日食求言，愿时为普州乐至令，应诏上言，极论时政凡万言，其大要有十：一曰谨始以正本，二 曰敬德以格天，三曰谨好恶以防小人，四曰审信任以辨君子，五曰开言路以来直谏，六曰详听言以观事实，七曰破党议以存至公，八曰登硕德以服天下，九曰从宽厚 以尽人才，十曰崇名节以厚士风。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfu, when an eclipse prompted a call for memorials, Yuan was then magistrate of Lezhi in Puzhou; he responded to the edict with a memorial of some ten thousand characters exhaustively discussing current affairs. Its main points were ten: first, be careful at the beginning to rectify the root; second, revere virtue to move Heaven; third, be careful in likes and dislikes to guard against petty men; fourth, examine trust to distinguish gentlemen; fifth, open the way for speech to welcome forthright remonstrance; sixth, examine words carefully to observe actual facts; seventh, break up factional disputes to preserve supreme fairness; eighth, elevate great virtue to win over the realm; ninth, follow leniency to exhaust human talent; tenth, honor reputation and integrity to strengthen the scholar's ethos.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfu, when an eclipse prompted a call for memorials, Yuan was then magistrate of Lezhi in Puzhou. He responded with a memorial of some ten thousand characters exhaustively discussing current affairs. Its ten main points were: be careful at the beginning to rectify the root; revere virtue to move Heaven; be careful in likes and dislikes to guard against petty men; examine trust to distinguish gentlemen; open the way for speech to welcome forthright remonstrance; examine words carefully to observe actual facts; break up factional disputes to preserve supreme fairness; elevate great virtue to win over the realm; follow leniency to exhaust human talent; and honor reputation and integrity to strengthen the scholar's ethos.

sentences.zh: 疏上不报。

translations.literal: The memorial received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 崇宁元年，诏籍元祐、元符上书人姓名，愿以选人籍入邪下等，谪监华州西岳庙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, an edict registered the names of Yuanyou and Yuanfu memorial submitters; Yuan was entered in the evil lower registry as a selected candidate and demoted to supervise the Western Peak Temple of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning, an edict registered the names of Yuanyou and Yuanfu memorial submitters. Yuan was entered in the evil lower registry as a selected candidate and demoted to supervise the Western Peak Temple of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 时当改京秩，迄不改，禁锢不调凡十 年。

translations.literal: It was time for promotion to capital rank, yet he was never promoted; the ban barred reassignment for ten years in all.
translations.idiomatic: It was time for promotion to capital rank, yet he was never promoted; the ban barred reassignment for ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 大观四年，孛星出，降赦，党禁解，始改秩，调知双流县。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daguang, a comet appeared, an amnesty was granted, and the party prohibition was lifted; he was finally promoted and assigned to govern Shuangliu County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daguang, a comet appeared, an amnesty was granted, and the party prohibition was lifted. He was finally promoted and assigned to govern Shuangliu County.

sentences.zh: 通判文州。

translations.literal: Supervising Prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as supervising prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡守郑行纯凭内侍势自恣，罢蕃夷互市，启边隙。

translations.literal: Prefect Zheng Xingchun relied on eunuch power to act willfully, abolished trade with tribal peoples at the frontier, and opened border tensions.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zheng Xingchun relied on eunuch power to act willfully, abolished trade with tribal peoples at the frontier, and opened border tensions.

sentences.zh: 愿争之，不从，径下令复其旧。

translations.literal: Yuan disputed it; the prefect would not listen, so Yuan directly ordered restoration of the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan disputed it; the prefect would not listen, so Yuan directly ordered the old practice restored.

sentences.zh: 守怒， 交章互奏，俱报罢。

translations.literal: The prefect was angry; they exchanged mutual impeachment memorials, and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was angry; they exchanged mutual impeachment memorials, and both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 而愿以曾入党籍，谪英州酒税，量移黄州，数年始予祠。

translations.literal: Because Yuan had been on the party registry, he was demoted to liquor tax at Yingzhou, transferred to Huangzhou, and only after several years was he granted an abbey stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan had been on the party registry, he was demoted to liquor tax at Yingzhou, transferred to Huangzhou, and only after several years was he granted an abbey stipend.

sentences.zh: 兴元帅臣王庶荐自代，通判果州。

translations.literal: Campaign commander Wang Shu recommended Yuan to succeed him; Supervising Prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commander Wang Shu recommended Yuan to succeed him, and he served as supervising prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，左丞冯澥荐备谏列，除开封府工曹，京城失 守，不克赴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, Left Vice Director Feng Xi recommended him for the remonstrance offices; he was appointed Opening Capital Works Officer, but when the capital fell he could not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingkang, Left Vice Director Feng Xi recommended him for the remonstrance offices. He was appointed opening capital works officer, but when the capital fell he could not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，擢知阆州。

translations.literal: After Gaozong crossed south, he was promoted to govern Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong crossed south, he was promoted to govern Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 会张浚谋大举，愿谓浚厉兵足谷以俟机会，浚不悦，以便旨移彭州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun planned a major campaign, Yuan urged Jun to sharpen troops and fill granaries awaiting opportunity; Jun was displeased and transferred him to Pengzhou by special edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun planned a major campaign, Yuan urged him to sharpen troops and fill granaries while awaiting opportunity. Jun was displeased and transferred him to Pengzhou by special edict.

sentences.zh: 有论边防书，名曰《罪言》。

translations.literal: He wrote a treatise on frontier defense called Words of Blame.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a treatise on frontier defense called Words of Blame.

sentences.zh: 守彭之明年，乞骸骨以归， 卒。

translations.literal: The year after governing Peng, he requested return on grounds of old age and died.
translations.idiomatic: The year after he took up office in Pengzhou, he requested to retire on grounds of old age and died.

sentences.zh: 方苏辙之读愿策，谓愿少年能不为进取计，异时当以直道闻，恨不及见，辙之言至是而验。

translations.literal: When Su Zhe read Yuan's examination answer, he said the young man could set aside advancement and would in time be known for the upright way; he regretted not living to see it. Zhe's words were now fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Zhe read Yuan's examination answer, he said the young man could set aside advancement and would in time be known for the upright way; he regretted not living to see it. Zhe's words were now fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 淳祐间，愿曾孙大酉侍讲经筵，因从容及之，上改容嘉叹，宣取所上书，又亲书“西社同门友，元符上书人”十大字以赐。

translations.literal: During the Chunyou era, Yuan's great-grandson Dayou served lecturing at the Classics Hall; the emperor changed expression and praised, ordered retrieval of his memorial, and personally wrote ten characters: "Fellow of Western Community, Yuanfu Memorial Submitter."
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunyou era, Yuan's great-grandson Dayou served lecturing at the Classics Hall. The emperor changed expression and praised him, ordered retrieval of the memorial, and personally wrote ten characters: "Fellow of Western Community, Yuanfu Memorial Submitter."

sentences.zh: 愿同郡杨恂，丹棱人也，字信仲。

translations.literal: Yang Xun of the same commandery as Yuan, from Danling, style name Xinzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xun of the same commandery as Yuan, from Danling, courtesy name Xinzhong.

sentences.zh: 元丰五年，登进士第。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元符初，知广都县，与愿同时上书，语甚切直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfu he governed Guangdu County and simultaneously memorialized with Yuan; his language was very forthright.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanfu he governed Guangdu County and simultaneously memorialized with Yuan; his language was very forthright.

sentences.zh: 越三年，亦同入党籍邪下第五等。

translations.literal: Three years later he also entered the party registry as evil fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he also entered the party registry as evil fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 其书以火不存。

translations.literal: His memorial was lost in a fire.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was lost in a fire.

sentences.zh: 张纲，字彦正，润州丹阳人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gang, style name Yanzheng, was a man of Danyang in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang, courtesy name Yanzheng, was a native of Danyang in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 入太学，以上舍及第。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy and passed as an upper hall graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy and passed as an upper hall graduate.

sentences.zh: 释褐，徽宗知纲三中首选，特除太学正，迁博士，除校书郎。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office, Emperor Huizong knew Gang had topped three sessions as first choice; he was specially appointed Hanlin Academy Instructor, promoted to Doctor, and appointed Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving office, Emperor Huizong knew Gang had topped three sessions as first choice. He was specially appointed Hanlin Academy instructor, promoted to doctor, and appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 入对，论：“君子小人簉殽，询言试事则邪正自 别。

translations.literal: At audience he argued, "When gentlemen and petty men are mixed together, inquiry and trial of affairs will naturally distinguish upright from perverse.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he argued, "When gentlemen and petty men are mixed together, inquiry and trial of affairs will naturally distinguish the upright from the perverse.

sentences.zh: 小人得志邀功生事，祸有不可胜言者。

translations.literal: When petty men gain their aim they invite merit and stir trouble—the disaster cannot all be told.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men gain their aim they invite merit and stir trouble—the disaster cannot all be told.

sentences.zh: 今用事者大言罔上，风俗侈靡，背本趋末，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Those in power today speak grandly and deceive above; custom is extravagant and wasteful, turning from root to tip, worsening day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power today speak grandly and deceive their superiors; custom grows ever more extravagant and wasteful, turning from root to tip, worsening day by day.

sentences.zh: 宜以祖考躬行之教为法，天下有不难化矣。

translations.literal: One ought to take the ancestors' personally practiced teaching as model—under Heaven would not be hard to transform.
translations.idiomatic: One ought to take the ancestors' personally practiced teaching as a model—then transforming the realm would not be difficult.

sentences.zh: ”上称善。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 论事与蔡京 不相合，挤之去，主管玉局观。

translations.literal: His policy views did not align with Cai Jing; Jing squeezed him out and placed him in charge of the Jade Bureau Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: His policy views did not align with Cai Jing; Jing forced him out and placed him in charge of the Jade Bureau Abbey.

sentences.zh: 久之还故官，兼修《国朝会要》、校正御前文字。

translations.literal: After a long time he was restored to his former post and also edited the Court Annals Compendium and corrected imperial texts.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was restored to his former post and also edited the Court Annals Compendium and corrected imperial texts.

sentences.zh: 迁著作佐郎、屯田司勋郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler and Director in the Ministries of Works and War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant compiler and director in the ministries of works and war.

sentences.zh: 初，朝议遣童贯、蔡攸使朔方，纲力论不 可出师状，不报。

translations.literal: Initially the court debated sending Tong Guan and Cai You as envoys north; Gang vigorously memorialized against dispatching troops, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the court debated sending Tong Guan and Cai You as envoys north. Gang vigorously memorialized against dispatching troops, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 及金渝盟犯京阙，命纲分守四壁，旋解严，诏登陴足月者迁。

translations.literal: When the Jin broke the treaty and invaded the capital, Gang was ordered to hold one of the four walls; soon the siege was lifted, and an edict said those who manned the walls a full month would be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin broke the treaty and invaded the capital, Gang was ordered to hold one of the four walls. Soon the siege was lifted, and an edict declared that those who manned the walls a full month would be promoted.

sentences.zh: 纲曰：“主忧臣辱，义当尔，顾因此受赏邪？

translations.literal: Gang said: "When the lord is troubled, the minister is disgraced; righteousness demands as much—yet would one accept reward on that account?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang said, "When the sovereign suffers, his ministers share the shame—it is only proper—but how could I accept a promotion for merely doing my duty?"

sentences.zh: ”卒不自言。

translations.literal: In the end he did not speak of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, he never spoke of his own service at all.

sentences.zh: 出为两浙提刑，移江东。

translations.literal: He was sent out as judicial intendant of the Two Zhes, then transferred to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial intendant of the Two Zhe circuits, then transferred to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 池将王进剽悍恣睢，曹官以小过违忤，遂钉手于门。

translations.literal: The Chizhou general Wang Jin was fierce and overbearing; a petty clerk, for a small offense that disobeyed and offended him, had his hands nailed to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, a general stationed at Chizhou, was brutally overbearing. When a petty clerk displeased him over a trifling matter, he had the man's hands nailed to the gate.

sentences.zh: 事闻，诏纲乘传穷竟。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the throne ordered Gang to travel by relay and investigate it thoroughly to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the emperor ordered Zhang Gang to ride post-haste and conduct a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 时国势未安，诸将往往易朝廷，进拥甲骑数百突至纲前，纲叱进阶下，即按问，罪立具， 自是无越法者。

translations.literal: At the time the state's situation was not settled; generals often looked lightly on the court. Jin, leading several hundred armored horsemen, burst forward to Gang. Gang shouted at him to come down from his horse, then immediately conducted the inquiry—the crime was established on the spot—and from then on none overstepped the law.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still unsettled, and many commanders held the court in contempt. Wang Jin rode up with several hundred armored cavalry and confronted Zhang Gang directly. Gang ordered him off his horse at once and questioned him; the charge was established on the spot. After that, no one in the region dared violate the law.

sentences.zh: 以左司召，权监察御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Left Assistant and appointed acting censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Left Assistant and appointed acting censor.

sentences.zh: 请令郡邑月具系囚存亡数，申提刑司，岁终校多寡行殿最。

translations.literal: He requested that counties and prefectures each month compile the numbers of prisoners held and whether they survived, submit them to the judicial intendant's office, and at year's end compare the totals and rank officials accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that every county and prefecture report monthly on detainees and whether they were alive or dead, submit these figures to the judicial intendant's office, and have officials ranked at year's end according to how well they had managed their prisons.

sentences.zh: 进起居舍人，改中书舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to recorder of attendance, then transferred to drafting secretary of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to recorder in attendance, then transferred to drafting secretary at the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 建言乞依祖宗法命大臣兼领史事，诏 宰臣吕颐浩监修国史，著为令。

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal asking that, in accord with ancestral law, high ministers be ordered concurrently to oversee historical affairs; an edict ordered chief minister Lü Yihao to supervise compilation of the national history, and this was established as a standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that, following ancestral precedent, senior ministers be ordered to oversee the historical records. The court commanded Grand Councilor Lü Yihao to supervise compilation of the National History and made this a standing rule.

sentences.zh: 试给事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting receptionist in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting receptionist in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大将有以军中田不均乞不收租，朝廷将从之，纲执不可。

translations.literal: A great general, on grounds that farmland within the army was uneven, requested that rents not be collected; the court was about to assent, but Gang steadfastly held it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: A senior commander asked that rent collection be waived on unequal military farmlands. The court was prepared to agree, but Zhang Gang insisted it could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 会推恩元祐党籍家，有司无限制，自陈者纷至。

translations.literal: It happened that grace was extended to families on the Yuanyou partisan list; the responsible offices set no limits, and those who came forward on their own testimony streamed in endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: As the court extended clemency to families implicated in the Yuanyou partisan list, the responsible offices imposed no clear limits, and claimants swarmed forward by the score.

sentences.zh: 纲 建议以崇宁所刻九十八人为正。

translations.literal: Gang recommended taking the ninety-eight persons carved at Chongning as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang advised that the ninety-eight names recorded on the Chongning stele be taken as the authoritative list.

sentences.zh: 自军兴后，小人多乘时召乱，历五年而怨家告讦者众。

translations.literal: Since the army's rise to action, petty men often seized the time to stir disorder; over five years, those with grudges lodging accusations became numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Since the war began, unscrupulous men had repeatedly stirred trouble in the chaos. After five years, vindictive accusers had become legion.

sentences.zh: 纲谓非所以广好生之德，乞自蔽囚，后有告勿受。

translations.literal: Gang said this was not the way to extend the virtue of cherishing life; he requested that from those already held in confinement onward, later accusations not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang argued that this undercut the sovereign's mercy and asked that, for all prisoners already in custody, no new denunciations be accepted.

sentences.zh: 宗室令懬特转太中大夫，纲 言：“庶官超转侍从非法，且自崇宁以来官职不循资任，致纲纪大坏，今方丕变其俗，奈何以令懬故复违旧章。

translations.literal: A clansman, Ling Kuan, was specially transferred to Grand Master of Palace Attendance; Gang said: "For common officials to leap to appointment among attendants is against law, and since Chongning offices have not followed qualifications and duties, causing the great ruin of discipline—now we are just greatly changing this custom—how can we, on Ling Kuan's account, again violate old statutes?"
translations.idiomatic: A member of the imperial clan, Ling Kuan, was specially promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance. Zhang Gang protested, "It is unlawful for a common official to skip directly into the ranks of palace attendants. Since the Chongning era, appointments have ignored seniority and qualifications, ruining public order. We are only now trying to change that habit—how can we break the old rules again for Ling Kuan's sake?"

sentences.zh: ”诏以次官命词，舍人王居正复执不行，命遂寝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered drafting the appointment document at the next lower rank; drafting secretary Wang Juzheng again steadfastly refused to carry it out, and the order was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the appointment drafted at a lower rank instead, but drafting secretary Wang Juzheng again refused to issue it, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 宣 抚使张俊驻师九江，遣营卒以书至瑞昌，县令郭彦章揣知卒与狱囚通，乃械系之。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Zhang Jun stationed troops at Jiujiang and sent a camp soldier with a letter to Ruichang; Magistrate Guo Yanzhao inferred the soldier was in collusion with prison inmates and had him shackled and detained.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Zhang Jun was encamped at Jiujiang and sent a camp runner bearing a letter to Ruichang. Magistrate Guo Yanzhao suspected the man was colluding with prisoners and had him arrested in irons.

sentences.zh: 俊酝于朝，彦章坐免。

translations.literal: Jun brought accusations at court, and Yanzhao was dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun lodged complaints at court, and Guo Yanzhao was dismissed as a result.

sentences.zh: 纲言：“近时州县吏多献谀当路，彦章不随流俗，是能奉法 守职，今不奖而黜，何以示劝？

translations.literal: Gang said: "In recent times county and prefecture clerks often offer flattery to those in power; Yanzhao did not follow the current fashion—this is ability to uphold law and keep office; now not rewarding but dismissing—how can encouragement be shown?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang argued, "These days local officials flatter the powerful at every turn. Guo Yanzhao refused to go along with the crowd and upheld the law. If the court dismisses rather than rewards him, what example does that set?"

sentences.zh: 除给事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed receptionist in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed receptionist in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 侍御史魏矼劾纲，提举太平观。

translations.literal: Attending censor Wei Kang impeached Gang, and he was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Wei Kang impeached Zhang Gang, who was then assigned to superintend the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 进徽猷阁待制，引年致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Huaiyou Pavilion academician-in-waiting and, citing age, retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician-in-waiting at the Huaiyou Pavilion and retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 秦桧用事久，纲卧家二十年绝不与通问。

translations.literal: Qin Hui held power for a long time; Gang lay at home for twenty years and absolutely did not exchange communications with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui dominated the court for years, Zhang Gang lived in retirement at home for twenty years and refused all contact with him.

sentences.zh: 桧 死，召为吏部侍郎兼侍读。

translations.literal: When Qin died, Gang was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui's death, Zhang Gang was recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrent palace reader.

sentences.zh: 初讲《诗关雎》，因后妃淑女事，历陈文王用人，寓意规戒。

translations.literal: When he first lectured on the "Guanju" ode of the Book of Poetry, he took the matter of the queen and virtuous ladies and, in sequence, set forth how King Wen employed men, intending admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: When he first lectured on the "Guanju" ode from the Book of Poetry, he used the theme of the queen and virtuous consorts to expound at length on how King Wen chose his ministers, offering implicit counsel and warning.

sentences.zh: 上曰：“久不闻博雅之言，今日所讲析理精详，深启朕心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It has been long since I have heard such learned discourse; what was lectured today analyzed principles with fine detail and deeply opened my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It has been a long time since I heard such erudite counsel. Today's lecture analyzed its subject with great precision and truly enlightened me."

sentences.zh: ”纲言：“比年 监司资浅望轻，请择七品以上清望官，或曾任郡守有治状者为之，庶位望既重，材能已试，可举其职。

translations.literal: Gang said: "In recent years circuit intendants have been shallow in qualification and light in standing; I request selecting clear-reputation officials of seventh rank and above, or those who have served as prefects with records of good governance, for these posts, so that once rank and standing are weighty and talent has already been tested, they may fulfill their duties."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang said, "In recent years the circuit intendants have been men of little seniority and standing. I ask that the court choose officials of seventh rank or above who enjoy a reputation for integrity, or former prefects with proven records of governance. Only when their rank and standing are weighty, and their ability already tested, can they truly perform the office."

sentences.zh: ”从之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 权吏部尚书。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 时以彗出东方，诏求言。

translations.literal: At the time a comet appeared in the east, and an edict sought opinions.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet appeared in the eastern sky, the emperor issued an edict soliciting memorials.

sentences.zh: 纲奏：“求言 易，听察难。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized: "Seeking opinions is easy; listening and examining is hard."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang memorialized, "It is easy to ask for opinions; it is hard to listen carefully and investigate them."

sentences.zh: 宜命有司详审章奏，必究极其情，无事苟简。

translations.literal: One should order the responsible offices to examine memorials in detail, necessarily reaching to the utmost of the facts, and not treat matters perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that the responsible offices review memorials thoroughly, investigate each matter to the full extent of the facts, and never treat submissions perfunctorily.

sentences.zh: ”除参知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 高宗频谕辅臣宽恤民力，盖惩秦桧苛政，期安黎庶。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong repeatedly instructed the chief ministers to relieve and soothe the people's burdens, intending to punish Qin Hui's harsh governance and bring peace to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong repeatedly urged his chief ministers to lighten the people's burdens, seeking to undo Qin Hui's harsh rule and restore peace to the populace.

sentences.zh: 纲乃摘其切于利民八十事，标以大 指，乞镂版宣布中外，于是人皆昭知上德意。

translations.literal: Gang then selected eighty matters most pressing for benefiting the people, marked them with main headings, and requested they be carved on blocks and proclaimed within and without; thus everyone clearly knew the emperor's virtuous intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang then distilled eighty measures most urgent for the people's welfare, summarized them under main headings, and asked that they be carved on printing blocks and promulgated throughout the realm, so that all might clearly understand the emperor's benevolent intent.

sentences.zh: 告老，以资政殿学士知婺州，寻致仕。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age and was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Wuzhou, then soon retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire on grounds of age, was made Academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Wuzhou, and soon retired from office.

sentences.zh: 高宗幸建康，纲朝行宫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong visited Jiankang, Gang attended at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong visited Jiankang, Zhang Gang presented himself at the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 孝宗登极，召纲陪祀南郊，以老辞不至，诏嘉之，命所 在州郡恒存问，仍赐羊酒，卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Gang was summoned to assist at the southern suburban sacrifice; citing age, he declined to come. An edict praised him, ordered the prefecture where he lived to inquire after him regularly, and still granted him mutton and wine. He died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne, Zhang Gang was summoned to assist at the southern suburban sacrifice. He declined on grounds of age. The court commended him, ordered his local prefecture to inquire after him regularly, and continued to grant him mutton and wine. He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 纲尝书坐右曰：“以直行己，以正立朝，以静退高天下。

translations.literal: Gang once wrote at his seat to the right: "With uprightness conduct yourself, with rectitude stand in court, with quiet withdrawal hold yourself above the world."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang once wrote these words and kept them at his right hand: "Conduct yourself with integrity, stand in court with rectitude, and hold yourself above the world through quiet withdrawal."

sentences.zh: ”其笃守如此。

translations.literal: His steadfast adherence was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the steadfastness with which he held to his principles.

sentences.zh: 初谥文定，吏部尚书汪应辰论驳之，孙釜再请，特赐曰章简。

translations.literal: His initial posthumous title was Wendi; Minister of Personnel Wang Yingchen disputed it, Sun Fu petitioned again, and he was specially granted the title Zhangjian.
translations.idiomatic: His initial posthumous title was Wendi, but Minister of Personnel Wang Yingchen objected. When Sun Fu petitioned again, the court specially granted him the title Zhangjian.

sentences.zh: 釜，庆元间为谏官，力排道学诸贤，累官至签书枢密院事。

translations.literal: Fu, during the Qingyuan era, served as remonstrance official, forcefully opposed the scholars of the Way, and rose through offices to Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu served as a remonstrance official during the Qingyuan era, vigorously opposed the Neo-Confucian scholars, and eventually rose to Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 张大经

translations.literal: Zhang Dajing
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajing

sentences.zh: 张大经，字彦文，建昌南城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dajing, courtesy name Yanwen, was a native of Nancheng in Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dajing, courtesy name Yanwen, was a native of Nancheng in Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 绍兴十五年，中进士第，宰吉之龙泉，有善政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of the Shaoxing era, he passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Longquan in Ji Prefecture, and had good policies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing, he passed the jinshi examination and served as magistrate of Longquan in Ji Prefecture, where he governed well.

sentences.zh: 诸司列荐，赐对便殿，出知仪真。

translations.literal: Various offices jointly recommended him; he was granted audience in the Hall of Convenience and was sent out as prefect of Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Various offices jointly recommended him. He was granted audience in the Hall of Convenience and was appointed prefect of Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 时两淮监司、帅守多兴事邀功，大经独以平易近 民，民咸德之。

translations.literal: At the time the circuit intendants and military commissioners of the Two Huai often undertook projects to invite merit; Dajing alone was close to the people and easy in governance, and the people all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, circuit intendants and military commissioners in the Two Huai regions often launched projects to claim credit. Dajing alone governed in an accessible, people-friendly manner, and the populace deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 提举湖南常平，提点湖北刑狱，寻移江东。

translations.literal: He served as intendant of Hunan Ever-Normal Granaries, judicial intendant of Hubei, and was soon transferred to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as intendant of Hunan Ever-Normal Granaries and judicial intendant of Hubei, then was soon transferred to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 他路有巨豪犯法，狱久不竟，命移属大经。

translations.literal: On another circuit a great magnate violated the law; the case long went unresolved, and the court ordered it transferred to Dajing's jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In another circuit a powerful magnate had broken the law, and the case had dragged on unresolved. The court ordered it transferred to Dajing's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 豪挟权势求脱，大经卒正其罪。

translations.literal: The magnate, relying on power and influence, sought release; Dajing in the end corrected his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The magnate used his power and connections to seek release, but Dajing ultimately secured his conviction.

sentences.zh: 孝宗重风宪之选，命条上部使 者十人，上独可大经，召见，上曰：“朕十人中得卿一人，以卿风力峻整。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong valued selections for the censorate and ordered a list drawn up of ten senior envoys; the emperor alone approved Dajing. Summoned for audience, the emperor said: "Among my ten men I have obtained you alone, because your force of character is stern and upright."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong valued appointments to the censorate and ordered a list drawn up of ten senior envoys. The emperor singled out Dajing alone for approval. When summoned for audience, the emperor said, "Of the ten men on my list, you are the one I want—because your force of character is stern and upright."

sentences.zh: ”遂除监察御史，命下，中外耸叹。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed censor; when the order was issued, court and country alike marveled.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed censor. When the appointment was announced, it stirred admiration throughout court and country.

sentences.zh: 大经首陈士风掊克、偷惰、诞慢、浮虚 四弊。

translations.literal: Dajing first set forth four abuses of scholar-official conduct: extortion, sloth, insolence, and empty pretension.
translations.idiomatic: Dajing first identified four abuses afflicting scholar-official conduct: extortion, sloth, insolence, and empty pretension.

sentences.zh: 时理官间多居外，大经奏非便，乃作舍守庭。

translations.literal: At the time judicial officials often resided outside the capital; Dajing memorialized that this was inconvenient, and the practice of holding court in the office was instituted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many judicial officials worked outside the capital. Dajing memorialized that this was impractical, and the court instituted the practice of holding sessions within the judicial office.

sentences.zh: 迁大理少卿，守殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and retained his post as palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review while retaining his post as palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 言：“今日不治，由大臣不任责。

translations.literal: He said: "The reason the realm is not well governed today is that great ministers do not bear responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The reason the realm is poorly governed today is that the great ministers refuse to accept responsibility."

sentences.zh: ”又言：“诸路荒政不实，飞蝗颇多。

translations.literal: He also said: "Relief policies on the various circuits are not genuine, and locust swarms are quite numerous."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Famine relief on the various circuits is not being carried out honestly, and locust swarms are widespread."

sentences.zh: 愿益加恐 惧，申饬大臣，俾内而百官有司输忠谠、修厥职，外而监司守臣察贪理冤、去苛敛、宽民力。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to increase fear and caution still further, admonish the great ministers, and cause those within—the hundred officials and responsible offices—to offer loyal and forthright counsel and perform their duties, and those without—the circuit intendants and prefects—to investigate greed, settle wrongs, remove harsh levies, and lighten the people's burdens.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to redouble your caution, admonish the chief ministers, and require officials at court to offer loyal and forthright counsel and perform their duties, while circuit intendants and prefects investigate corruption, redress injustice, abolish harsh levies, and lighten the people's burdens.

sentences.zh: ”上皆嘉纳。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 因论近习韩俣荐士，上曰：“此亦无害。

translations.literal: In discussing the attendant Han Yu's recommendation of scholars, the emperor said: "This too is harmless."
translations.idiomatic: When the discussion turned to the attendant Han Yu recommending scholars, the emperor said, "There is no harm in that."

sentences.zh: 昔杨得意为狗 监，亦尝荐司马相如。

translations.literal: In former times Yang Deyi, as dog keeper, also once recommended Sima Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Yang Deyi, as keeper of the imperial hounds, also once recommended Sima Xiangru.

sentences.zh: ”大经奏：“彼何人斯，使得荐士，将恐无廉耻者望风希旨，伤毁士俗。

translations.literal: Dajing memorialized: "What sort of man is he, that he should be allowed to recommend scholars? I fear the shameless will look to the wind and seek to please, injuring and ruining scholar-official custom."
translations.idiomatic: Dajing memorialized, "What sort of man is this, that he should be allowed to recommend scholars? I fear the shameless will take their cue from him and seek favor by flattery, corrupting the standards of the scholar-official class."

sentences.zh: ”后数日，上谓大经曰：“卿前所论韩俣，朕思之诚是也。

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor said to Dajing: "What you previously said about Han Yu—I have reflected on it, and you are indeed right."
translations.idiomatic: Several days later the emperor told Dajing, "What you said earlier about Han Yu—I have thought it over, and you are entirely right."

sentences.zh: ”又论宦 者董琏暴横，将命淮甸，所至诛求，且自号“董阎罗”。

translations.literal: He also discussed the eunuch Dong Lian, violent and overbearing, who was about to be dispatched to the Huai region; wherever he went he extorted, and he even styled himself "Dong Yama."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke against the eunuch Dong Lian, a violent and overbearing man who was about to be dispatched to the Huai region. Wherever he went he extorted the people, and he even styled himself "Dong Yama."

sentences.zh: 上曰：“然，人皆言之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Indeed—everyone says so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Indeed—everyone says so."

sentences.zh: ”即依奏镌罢，窜南康军。

translations.literal: The court immediately followed the memorial, stripped him of office, and banished him to Nankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court immediately acted on the memorial, stripped Dong Lian of office, and banished him to Nankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 除侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed attending censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attending censor.

sentences.zh: 上宣谕曰：“卿论事得体，且详练。

translations.literal: The emperor announced and instructed: "Your memorials are appropriate in manner, and moreover detailed and practiced."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed him directly: "Your memorials are well judged in manner, and moreover thorough and informed."

sentences.zh: ”大经 遂言：“士风未厚，吏治未肃，民力未苏，和气未应，皆由人心未正。

translations.literal: Dajing then said: "Scholar-official custom is not yet thick, official governance is not yet disciplined, the people's strength is not yet restored, harmonious qi has not yet responded—all because human hearts are not yet upright."
translations.idiomatic: Dajing then said, "Scholar-official standards remain weak, official governance is still lax, the people's strength has not recovered, and harmonious responses have not come—all because hearts are not yet set right."

sentences.zh: 愿察公正，明义利，以彰好恶，抑浮薄，去贪刻，则莫不靡然洗濯，一归于正。

translations.literal: I wish to examine fairness and justice, clarify righteousness and profit, make good and evil manifest, suppress frivolity and superficiality, and remove greed and harshness—then none will fail to be thoroughly cleansed and return as one to the upright.
translations.idiomatic: I urge the court to examine fairness and justice, distinguish righteousness from profit, make good and evil clear, suppress frivolity, and remove greed and harshness—then all will be thoroughly cleansed and brought back to the upright path.

sentences.zh: ”上称善再 三。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it good again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his words repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 又言：“监司治民之本，不可限以资格。

translations.literal: He also said: "Circuit intendants are the foundation of governing the people and cannot be limited by qualifications."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Circuit intendants are the foundation of governing the people and cannot be chosen by rigid qualification alone."

sentences.zh: ”上纳其言，即选四寺丞同时临遣。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and immediately selected four assistant commissioners of the Court of Judicial Review and dispatched them at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and immediately selected four assistant commissioners of the Court of Judicial Review and dispatched them on circuit at once.

sentences.zh: 试右谏议大夫兼侍讲。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting Right Remonstrance Official and concurrent palace lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Right Remonstrance Official and concurrent palace lecturer.

sentences.zh: 请通漕臣之计，以补州郡之有无；

translations.literal: He requested coordinating the plans of transport commissioners to supplement what prefectures and commanderies lacked or possessed;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed coordinating transport commissioners' plans to balance what prefectures and commanderies lacked against what they possessed;

sentences.zh: 拘户绝之租，以广常平之 储侍；

translations.literal: seizing rents from extinct households to expand ever-normal granary reserves;
translations.idiomatic: collecting rents from extinct households to expand ever-normal granary reserves;

sentences.zh: 严脏罪改正法，以惩贪黩；

translations.literal: strictly enforcing the law on correcting corruption offenses to punish greed and misconduct;
translations.idiomatic: strictly enforcing the law on corruption to punish greed and misconduct;

sentences.zh: 收外路辟阙归吏部，以杜私谒而通孤寒。

translations.literal: recalling outside appointments made by special selection to the Ministry of Personnel, to block private petitions and open the way for the isolated and poor.
translations.idiomatic: returning appointments made by special selection outside the capital to the Ministry of Personnel, to block private petitions and open the way for the isolated and poor.

sentences.zh: 秋旱，诏求言。

translations.literal: In an autumn drought, an edict sought opinions.
translations.idiomatic: During an autumn drought, the emperor issued an edict soliciting memorials.

sentences.zh: 大经极言：“人心不和有以致之。

translations.literal: Dajing spoke to the utmost: "There are causes that lead human hearts to disharmony."
translations.idiomatic: Dajing spoke forcefully: "There are causes that have led human hearts into disharmony."

sentences.zh: 民力竭而愁叹多，军士 贫而怨嗟众，二者当今大弊。

translations.literal: The people's strength is exhausted and lamentation is many; soldiers are poor and resentment is widespread—these two are the great abuses of the present day.
translations.idiomatic: The people's strength is exhausted and their lamentations are many; soldiers are impoverished and their resentments widespread—these two are the great abuses of the day.

sentences.zh: 州县之间，绢帛多折其估，米粟过收其赢，关市苛征，榷酤峻禁。

translations.literal: Between prefectures and counties, silk is often discounted in valuation, grain and rice are over-collected for surplus, transit markets are harshly taxed, and monopoly wine is strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Between prefectures and counties, silk is often undervalued in assessment, grain is over-collected for surplus profit, transit markets are harshly taxed, and wine monopolies are rigidly enforced.

sentences.zh: 中外兵帅多出贵幸之门，营利自丰，素召众怨，教阅灭裂，军容不 整。

translations.literal: Military commanders within and without mostly come from the gates of the noble and favored; they enrich themselves through profit and ordinarily invite widespread resentment; training and review are perfunctory, and military appearance is not in order.
translations.idiomatic: Military commanders inside and outside the capital mostly come from noble and favored households. They enrich themselves through profit, invite widespread resentment, conduct perfunctory training and review, and keep their forces in poor order.

sentences.zh: 且近习甲第名园，越法逾制，别墅列肆，在在有之，非赂遗何以济欲？

translations.literal: Moreover, the favored attendants' mansions and famous gardens exceed law and regulation, and villas and shops are everywhere—how can desires be satisfied without bribes and gifts?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the favored attendants maintain mansions and famous gardens that exceed law and regulation, and their villas and shops are everywhere—how can such desires be satisfied without bribes and gifts?

sentences.zh: 愿陛下疏斥憸腐，抑绝幸门，垂意人主之职，责成宰辅，一提其纲，则天下事必有能办之 者。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to dismiss and reject the crafty and corrupt, suppress and cut off the gates of favor, turn attention to the duties of the sovereign, hold the chief ministers accountable, and once the guiding rope is lifted, then affairs under heaven will surely have those able to handle them.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to dismiss the crafty and corrupt, shut the gates of favor, attend to the sovereign's own duties, hold the chief ministers accountable, and once the guiding rope is lifted, there will surely be those under heaven able to handle the realm's affairs.

sentences.zh: ”俄而池司郝政降充统制官，殿帅补外，盖用其言也。

translations.literal: Before long Chi Prefecture official Hao Zheng was demoted to serve as a command officer, and the palace commander was reassigned outside the capital—this was putting his words into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Chi Prefecture official Hao Zheng was demoted to command officer, and the palace commander was reassigned outside the capital—implementing his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 除礼部尚书兼侍读。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent palace reader.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent palace reader.

sentences.zh: 大经屡请祠，上曰：“卿公廉必能为朕牧民。

translations.literal: Dajing repeatedly requested a sinecure post; the emperor said: "You are upright and incorrupt and can surely govern the people for Us."
translations.idiomatic: Dajing repeatedly requested a sinecure post. The emperor said, "You are upright and incorrupt and can surely govern the people on my behalf."

sentences.zh: ”以徽猷阁学士知建宁 府。

translations.literal: He was made Huaiyou Pavilion academician and prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Huaiyou Pavilion academician and prefect of Jianning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未几，移镇绍兴，辞不拜，予祠。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to guard Shaoxing, declined to accept the appointment, and was granted a sinecure post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reassigned to Shaoxing, but he refused the post and was instead granted a ceremonial stipend.

sentences.zh: 进龙图阁学士，告老，以通奉大夫致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, petitioned to retire on account of age, and retired with the rank of Grand Master for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, he asked to retire and left office with the rank of Grand Master for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 方主眷未衰，抗疏引去，人方之孔戣。

translations.literal: Just when imperial favor had not yet waned, he submitted a memorial to withdraw from office; people compared him to Kong Kui.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor's favor was still strong, he submitted a memorial insisting on withdrawal, and people likened him to Kong Kui.

sentences.zh: 寿逾八袠，绍熙五年，宁宗即位，进正议大 夫，降诏抚问，赐银奁药茗。

translations.literal: Past eighty years of age, in the fifth year of Shaoxi when Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Remonstrance; an imperial edict was issued to console and inquire after him, and he was granted a silver casket of medicine and tea.
translations.idiomatic: He lived past eighty. In the fifth year of Shaoxi, when Emperor Ningzong took the throne, he was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Remonstrance; the court sent an edict of consolation and bestowed a silver casket of medicine and tea.

sentences.zh: 庆元四年七月，疾革，语诸子曰：“吾目可暝，吾爱君忧国之心不可泯。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Qingyuan, as his illness became critical, he told his sons, "My eyes may close, but my heart that loves the sovereign and grieves for the state cannot be extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Qingyuan, as his illness turned grave, he told his sons, "My eyes may close, but my love for the sovereign and my grief for the state will never die."

sentences.zh: ”无一语及私。

translations.literal: He did not utter a single word about private matters.
translations.idiomatic: He said nothing about personal affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 讣闻，上甚悼之，赠银青光禄 大夫，谥简肃。

translations.literal: When news of his death reached the throne, the emperor mourned him deeply, posthumously granted him the title of Grand Master of Silver and Blue Light, and gave him the posthumous name Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the throne, the emperor grieved deeply, posthumously ennobled him as Grand Master of Silver and Blue Light, and gave him the posthumous name Jiansu (Concise and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 蔡洸，字子平，其先兴化仙游人，端明殿学士襄之后，徙霅川。

translations.literal: Cai Guang, courtesy name Ziping, was originally from Xianyou in Xinghua—a descendant of Academician of the Hall of Duanming, Cai Xiang—the family later moved to Zhechuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Guang, courtesy name Ziping, came from a family originally of Xianyou in Xinghua, descended from the Duanming Hall academician Cai Xiang; the clan later moved to Zhechuan.

sentences.zh: 父伸，左中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Shen held the title of Left Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen served as Left Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 洸以荫补将仕郎，中法科，除大理评事，迁寺丞，出 知吉州。

translations.literal: Guang entered service through hereditary privilege as a General Gentleman-for-Service, passed the legal examinations, was appointed Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Vice Director of the court, and sent out as Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guang entered office by hereditary privilege as a General Gentleman-for-Service, passed the legal examinations, was made Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to Vice Director of the court, and appointed Prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 召为刑部郎，徙度支，以户部郎总领淮东军马钱粮、知镇江府。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to the Department of Revenue, and as a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue concurrently oversaw military funds and provisions for Huaidong while serving as Prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, then transferred to the Department of Revenue, he served as a Ministry of Revenue Secretary overseeing Huaidong military funds and provisions while governing Zhenjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 会西溪卒移屯建康，舳舻相衔。

translations.literal: When the Xixi garrison troops relocated to Jiankang, their boats stretched bow to stern in an unbroken line.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xixi garrison was transferred to Jiankang, boats lined up stem to stern along the river.

sentences.zh: 时久旱，郡民筑陂潴水灌溉，漕司檄郡决之，父老泣诉。

translations.literal: At a time of prolonged drought, the people of the prefecture had built a dam to hold water for irrigation; the transport commissioner ordered the prefecture to breach it, and the village elders came weeping to plead their case.
translations.idiomatic: During a long drought the people had built a dam to store water for irrigation, but the transport commissioner ordered the prefecture to break it open; the village elders came weeping to protest.

sentences.zh: 洸 曰：“吾不忍获罪百姓也。

translations.literal: Guang said, "I cannot bear to commit an offense against the people."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "I cannot bear to wrong the people."

sentences.zh: ”却之。

translations.literal: He refused the order.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 已而大雨，漕运通，岁亦大熟。

translations.literal: Before long heavy rain fell, transport routes reopened, and the harvest was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heavy rains came, transport routes opened again, and the year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 民歌之曰：“我潴我水，以灌以溉。

translations.literal: The people sang in praise, "We hold back our water to irrigate our fields."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang in praise: "We store our water to irrigate our fields."

sentences.zh: 俾我不夺，蔡公是赖。

translations.literal: That it was not taken from us, we owe to Master Cai.
translations.idiomatic: That we were not deprived of it, we owe to Master Cai.

sentences.zh: ”就除司农少卿，言：“镇江三邑税 户客户输丁各异，请为一体，不得自为同异。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Agriculture and memorialized, "In the three districts of Zhenjiang, tax households and tenant households render corvée labor contributions differently—I request they be unified and not allowed to differ on their own."
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Agriculture and memorialized: "In Zhenjiang's three districts, tax households and tenant households pay corvée levies differently. I ask that they be treated as one and not allowed to vary on their own."

sentences.zh: 所输丁绢，依和买之直，计尺折纳，人给一钞，官自买绢起发，公私皆便。

translations.literal: The labor silk paid in should be assessed at the hemai purchase price, calculated by length and collected in kind; each person would receive a certificate, and the government would buy the silk and dispatch it itself—convenient for both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Labor silk payments should be assessed at the hemai purchase price, measured by length and collected in kind; each person would receive a certificate, and the government would buy and ship the silk itself—benefiting both state and people.

sentences.zh: ”上嘉纳。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 以户部侍郎召，试吏部尚书，移 户部。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue, examined for appointment as Minister of Personnel, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue, he was examined for the post of Minister of Personnel and then transferred to head the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上谓侍臣曰：“朕以版曹得人为喜。

translations.literal: The emperor told his attending ministers, "I am pleased to have found the right man for the Ministry of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attending ministers, "I am delighted to have found the right man for the Ministry of Revenue."

sentences.zh: ”洸常言：“财无渗漏则不可胜用。

translations.literal: Guang often said, "If revenue has no leakages, it cannot but suffice for use."
translations.idiomatic: Guang often said, "If there are no leaks in the treasury, the funds will more than suffice."

sentences.zh: ”未几求去，除徽猷阁学士、知宁国府。

translations.literal: Before long he requested leave, was appointed Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning, and made Prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to leave office and was appointed Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and Prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 陛辞赐坐，上慰劳曰：“卿面有火色，风证 也，朕有二方赐卿。
