translations.literal: At his farewell audience he was granted a seat; the emperor comforted him, saying, "Your face shows a fiery flush—it is a wind ailment; I have two prescriptions to bestow upon you."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he was granted a seat. The emperor comforted him, saying, "Your face is flushed—it is a wind ailment. I have two prescriptions for you."

sentences.zh: ”洸谢，即奉祠以归。

translations.literal: Guang thanked him and immediately received a sinecure post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Guang thanked him, received a sinecure post, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 洸事亲孝，曾祖襄未易名，力请于朝，赐谥忠惠。

translations.literal: Guang was filial toward his parents; his great-grandfather Xiang had not had his posthumous name changed—he vigorously petitioned the court, and the posthumous name Zhonghui was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was filial to his parents. His great-grandfather Xiang had not yet received a revised posthumous name, so Guang pressed the court until the posthumous name Zhonghui (Loyal and Kind) was granted.

sentences.zh: 所得奉，每以振亲戚之贫者，去朝之日，囊无餘资，至售所赐银鞍鞯治行，人服其清洁云。

translations.literal: His salary he always used to aid impoverished relatives; on the day he left the capital his purse held nothing extra—even selling his granted silver saddle and tack to fund his journey. People admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He used his salary to support poor relatives, and when he left the capital his purse was empty—he even sold the silver saddle and tack the court had granted him to pay for the journey. People admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 莫濛字子蒙，湖州归安人。

translations.literal: Mo Meng, courtesy name Zimeng, was a native of Gui'an in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Meng, courtesy name Zimeng, was a native of Gui'an in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 以祖荫补将仕郎，两魁法科，累官至大理评事、提举广南市舶。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's privilege he entered as General Gentleman-for-Service, twice topped the legal examinations, and rose through the ranks to Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review and Commissioner of Guangnan Maritime Trade.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather's privilege he entered as General Gentleman-for-Service, twice topped the legal examinations, and rose to Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review and Commissioner of Guangnan Maritime Trade.

sentences.zh: 张子华以脏败，朝廷命濛往鞫之，濛正其罪。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zihua was disgraced for corruption, the court sent Meng to investigate him, and Meng upheld his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zihua was ruined by a corruption scandal, the court sent Meng to investigate, and Meng confirmed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 又言秦熺、郑时中受子华 赂，计直数千缗。

translations.literal: He also reported that Qin Xi and Zheng Shizhong had accepted bribes from Zihua worth several thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Qin Xi and Zheng Shizhong had taken bribes from Zihua worth several thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 还朝，除大理寺正。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 吏部火，连坐者数百人，久不决，命濛治之。

translations.literal: When fire broke out in the Ministry of Personnel, hundreds were implicated and the case long unresolved—the court ordered Meng to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the Ministry of Personnel, hundreds were implicated and the case dragged on unresolved until the court put Meng in charge.

sentences.zh: 濛察其最可疑者留于狱，出餘人为耳目以踪迹之，约三日复来，遂得其实，系者 乃得释。

translations.literal: Meng identified the most suspicious, kept them in prison, released the rest as informants to track leads, set a deadline of three days for their return, and thus got the truth—the wrongly detained were released.
translations.idiomatic: Meng kept the most suspicious in custody, released the rest to serve as informants, set a three-day deadline for them to return with evidence, and thus uncovered the truth so the wrongly detained could go free.

sentences.zh: 黄州卒奏亲擒盗五十餘人，上命濛穷竟，既至，咸以冤告。

translations.literal: A soldier from Huangzhou reported personally capturing over fifty bandits; the emperor ordered Meng to fully investigate—upon arrival, all pleaded wrongful accusation.
translations.idiomatic: A Huangzhou soldier reported that he had personally captured more than fifty bandits; the emperor ordered Meng to investigate thoroughly, and upon arrival all the accused pleaded that they had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 濛命囚去桎梏，引卒至庭，询窃发之由，斗敌之所，远近时日悉皆牴牾，折之，语塞。

translations.literal: Meng had the prisoners freed from shackles, summoned the soldier to court, questioned the circumstances of the theft, fighting places, distances and times—all contradicted; pressed, the soldier was speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Meng removed the prisoners' shackles, brought the soldier into court, and questioned him about where the theft occurred, where the fight took place, and the distances and times involved—every detail contradicted the rest; pressed further, the soldier had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 濛具正犯 数人奏上，余释之。

translations.literal: Meng submitted a report naming only the actual offenders and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Meng reported only the true offenders to the throne and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 上谕辅臣曰：“莫濛非独晓刑狱，可俾理金谷。

translations.literal: The emperor told his chief ministers, "Mo Meng understands not only criminal law—he can be entrusted with managing fiscal affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers, "Mo Meng understands more than criminal law—he can be entrusted with managing the treasury."

sentences.zh: ”除户部员外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣濛措置浙西、江淮沙田芦场，上语之曰：“得此可助经 费，归日以版曹处卿。

translations.literal: The court sent Meng to organize sandy fields and reed marshes in Zhexi and the Jianghuai region; the emperor told him, "Gains here can help with expenses—upon your return I shall place you at the Ministry of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Meng to organize sandy fields and reed marshes in Zhexi and the Jianghuai region. The emperor told him, "Revenue from this can help with expenses—when you return I shall place you in the Ministry of Revenue."

sentences.zh: ”濛多方括责，得二百五十三万七千餘亩。

translations.literal: Meng assessed through many methods and obtained over 2,537,000 mu.
translations.idiomatic: Meng assessed the land by many methods and registered more than 2,537,000 mu.

sentences.zh: 言者论其丈量失实，征收及贫民，责监饶州景德镇。

translations.literal: Criticism was raised that his surveying was inaccurate and collection reached the poor; he was punished by supervision duty at Jingdezhen in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged that his surveying was inaccurate and that collection fell on the poor; he was demoted to supervisory duty at Jingdezhen in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 起知光化军。

translations.literal: He was reinstated as military prefect of Guanghua.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as military prefect of Guanghua.

sentences.zh: 谍知金渝盟，郡乏舟，众以为 虑，濛力为办集，及敌犯境，民赖以济。

translations.literal: Intelligence revealed the Jin would break the treaty; the commandery lacked boats and many worried—but Meng worked hard to gather them, and when enemies invaded the border the people were saved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence showed the Jin would break the treaty. The commandery lacked boats and many were alarmed, but Meng worked hard to gather them, and when the enemy crossed the border the people were saved.

sentences.zh: 时饷馈急，除淮南转运判官，濛迁延不之任，右司谏梁仲敏劾其慢命，罢官勒停。

translations.literal: When supplies were urgently needed, he was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan, but Meng delayed taking office; Right Remonstrance Official Liang Zhongmin impeached him for disobedience and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When supplies were urgently needed he was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of Huainan, but Meng delayed taking up the post; Right Remonstrance Official Liang Zhongmin impeached him for insubordination and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣谕使汪澈为言于上，复旧职，召见，上 谕曰：“朕常记向措置沙田甚不易。

translations.literal: Imperial Commissioner Wang Che spoke on his behalf to the emperor; his former post was restored and he was summoned—the emperor said, "I often recall how hard your sand-field project was."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Commissioner Wang Che pleaded his case before the emperor; his former post was restored and he was summoned to audience. The emperor said, "I often remember how difficult your sand-field project was."

sentences.zh: 濛谢曰：“职尔，不敢避怨。

translations.literal: Meng replied in thanks, "It was my duty—I dared not shun ill will."
translations.idiomatic: Meng replied, "It was my duty—I dared not shun resentment."

sentences.zh: ”上曰：“使任责者人人如卿，天下何事不成。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If every person entrusted with responsibility were like you, what in the realm could not be accomplished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If everyone entrusted with responsibility were like you, what in the realm could not be accomplished?"

sentences.zh: 除湖北转运判官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 未几，知鄂州，召除户部左曹郎中，出知扬州。

translations.literal: Soon Prefect of Ezhou, recalled and appointed Director of the Left Section of the Ministry of Revenue, then sent out as Prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Prefect of Ezhou, he was recalled and appointed Director of the Left Section of the Ministry of Revenue, then sent out again as Prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陛辞，上以城圮，命濛增筑。

translations.literal: At farewell audience the emperor noted the walls were ruined and ordered Meng to rebuild them.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor noted that the city walls were in ruins and ordered Meng to rebuild them.

sentences.zh: 濛至州，规度城，分授诸将各刻姓名甃堞间，县重赏激劝，阅数月告成。

translations.literal: Arriving at the prefecture, Meng surveyed the wall, assigned each general a section with names carved on the parapets, posted heavy rewards as incentive, and within months completion was announced.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture, Meng surveyed the walls, assigned each general a section with names carved on the parapets, offered heavy rewards as incentive, and within months the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 除直宝文阁学 士、大理少卿兼详定司敕令官，兼权知临安府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review concurrently Compiler of Statutes and Decrees, with concurrent acting Prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and Compiler of Statutes and Decrees, with concurrent acting Prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 未几，假工部尚书使金贺正旦。

translations.literal: Soon acting as Minister of Works on an embassy to Jin to congratulate the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he served as acting Minister of Works on an embassy to Jin to congratulate the New Year.

sentences.zh: 金庭锡宴，濛以本朝忌日不敢簪花听乐，金遣人趣赴，濛坚执不从，竟不能夺。

translations.literal: At a Jin court banquet Meng refused flowers and music because it was a mourning day in the Song calendar; Jin envoys urged him to attend but he steadfastly refused and could not be moved.
translations.idiomatic: At a Jin court banquet Meng refused flowers and music because it was a day of mourning in the Song calendar; Jin envoys pressed him to join, but he steadfastly refused and could not be moved.

sentences.zh: 使 还，除刑部侍郎，改工部侍郎兼临安府少尹，以言者罢。

translations.literal: Returning from the mission, appointed Vice Minister of Justice, changed to Vice Minister of Works concurrently Junior Prefect of Lin'an—dismissed due to criticism.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the mission he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice, then Vice Minister of Works and Junior Prefect of Lin'an, but was dismissed after criticism from memorialists.

sentences.zh: 起知鄂州。

translations.literal: He was reinstated as Prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reinstated as Prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，年六十一，赠正奉大夫。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-one; posthumously granted Grand Master for Direct Administration.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at the age of sixty-one and was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Master for Direct Administration.

sentences.zh: 周淙，字彦广，湖州长兴人。

translations.literal: Zhou Cong, courtesy name Yanguang, was a native of Changxing in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Cong, courtesy name Yanguang, was a native of Changxing in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 父需，以进士起 家，官至左中奉大夫。

translations.literal: His father Xu began from the jinshi degree and rose to Left Grand Master for Direct Administration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu entered office through the jinshi degree and rose to Left Grand Master for Direct Administration.

sentences.zh: 淙幼警敏，力学，宣和间以父任为郎，历官至通判建康府。

translations.literal: Cong was precocious and studious; in the Xuanhe era he entered as Gentleman through his father's position and rose to Vice Prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was precocious and devoted to study; in the Xuanhe era he entered office through his father's position and rose to Vice Prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 绍兴三十年，金渝盟，边事方兴，帅守难其选，士夫亦惮行。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing the Jin broke the treaty, border affairs newly arisen—hard to find military governors and officials feared going.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing the Jin broke the treaty and border affairs flared up; it was hard to find suitable commanders, and officials feared taking frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 首命淙守滁阳，未 赴，移楚州，又徙濠梁。

translations.literal: First ordered to guard Chuyang; before departing moved to Chuzhou, then transferred to Haoliang.
translations.idiomatic: He was first ordered to guard Chuyang; before he could take up the post he was moved to Chuzhou, then transferred to Haoliang.

sentences.zh: 淮、楚旧有并山水置砦自卫者，淙为立约束，结保伍。

translations.literal: In Huai and Chu there were locals who built fortresses using terrain for self-defense—Cong established regulations and organized mutual aid groups.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huai and Chu regions people had long built mountain fortresses for self-defense; Cong established regulations and organized mutual-aid groups.

sentences.zh: 金主亮倾国犯边，民赖以全活者不可胜计。

translations.literal: When Jin ruler Hailing mobilized the whole state to invade, countless people survived thanks to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin emperor Hailing mobilized the whole country to invade the border, countless people survived because of him.

sentences.zh: 除直秘阁，再任。

translations.literal: Granted direct access to the Privy Archive, reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted direct access to the Privy Archive and reappointed.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禅，王师进取虹 县，中原之民翕然来归，扶老携幼相属于道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended, Song troops took Hong County and Central Plains people flocked home, old and young crowding the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Song troops advanced to take Hong County, and people of the Central Plains came home in droves, the old and young crowding the roads.

sentences.zh: 淙计口给食，行者犒以牛酒，至者处以室庐，人人感悦。

translations.literal: Cong rationed food by headcount, rewarded travelers with oxen and wine, housed arrivals—all grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Cong rationed food by headcount, rewarded those on the road with oxen and wine, and housed those who arrived; everyone was grateful.

sentences.zh: 张浚视师，驻于都梁，见淙谋，辄称叹，且曰：“有急，公当 与我俱死。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun inspected troops at Duliang, praised Cong's plans, and said, "In crisis you must die with me."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun inspected the army at Duliang, praised Cong's plans, and said, "If there is an emergency, you must die with me."

sentences.zh: ”淙亦感激，至谓“头可断，身不可去”。

translations.literal: Cong was moved, declaring, "My head may be cut off but I will not leave."
translations.idiomatic: Cong was deeply moved and declared, "My head may be cut off, but I will not leave."

sentences.zh: 浚入朝，悉陈其状，上嘉叹不已，进直徽猷阁，帅维扬。

translations.literal: Zhang reported fully in court; the emperor praised endlessly, promoted Cong to the Hall of Splendid Learning, and made him military commissioner of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang reported the full situation in court; the emperor praised him repeatedly, promoted Cong to the Hall of Splendid Learning, and made him military commissioner of Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 会钱端礼以尚书宣谕淮东，复以淙荐， 进直显谟阁。

translations.literal: When Qian Duanli as Minister went as imperial commissioner to Huaidong and recommended Cong again, Cong was promoted to the Hall of Manifest Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Duanli went to Huaidong as Minister and imperial commissioner and recommended Cong again, Cong was promoted to the Hall of Manifest Counsel.

sentences.zh: 时两淮经践蹂，民多流亡，淙极力招辑，按堵如故。

translations.literal: Both Huai regions had been trampled; many displaced—but Cong gathered them and order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Both banks of the Huai had been ravaged and many people had fled, but Cong worked hard to gather and settle them until order was restored.

sentences.zh: 劝民植桑柘，开屯田，上亦专以属淙，屡赐亲札。

translations.literal: He urged planting mulberry and catalpa and opening military colonies; the emperor entrusted this solely to Cong with repeated personal letters.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the people to plant mulberry and catalpa and to open military colonies; the emperor entrusted this work solely to Cong and repeatedly sent him personal letters.

sentences.zh: 淙奉行益力，进直龙图阁，除两浙转运副使。

translations.literal: Cong worked harder still, promoted to the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of the Two Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Cong carried out the work with even greater energy, was promoted to the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, and appointed Transport Vice Commissioner of the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 未 几，知临安府，上言：“自古风化必自近始。

translations.literal: Soon Prefect of Lin'an, he memorialized, "Since antiquity moral transformation must begin close at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Prefect of Lin'an, he memorialized: "Since antiquity, moral transformation must begin close at hand."

sentences.zh: 陛下躬履节俭，以示四方，而贵近奢靡，殊不知革。

translations.literal: Your Majesty personally practices frugality to show the realm, yet the noble and near are lavish without reform.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally practices frugality to set an example for the realm, yet the nobles and those close to the throne remain extravagant and show no sign of reform.

sentences.zh: ”乃条上禁止十五事，上嘉纳之，降诏奖谕，赐金带。

translations.literal: He listed fifteen prohibitions; the emperor praised and adopted them, issued commendation, and granted a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a detailed list of fifteen prohibitions; the emperor praised and adopted them, issued an edict of commendation, and granted him a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 临安驻跸岁 久，居民日增，河流湫隘，舟楫病之，淙请疏浚。

translations.literal: Lin'an had long been the temporary capital; population grew, rivers silted and boats suffered—Cong requested dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Lin'an had long served as the temporary capital; as the population grew the rivers silted up and shipping suffered, so Cong requested dredging.

sentences.zh: 工毕，除秘阁修撰，进右文殿修撰，提举江州太平兴国宫以归。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he was appointed Compiler of the Privy Archive, promoted to Compiler of the Hall of Right Culture, placed in charge of Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he was appointed Compiler of the Privy Archive, promoted to Compiler of the Hall of Right Culture, placed in charge of Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 上念淙不忘，除敷文阁待制，起知宁国府，趣入 奏，上慰抚愈渥。

translations.literal: The emperor still thought of Cong; appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Spreading Culture, reinstated as Prefect of Ningguo, urged to report—comforted him warmly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still thought of Cong, appointed him Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Spreading Culture, reinstated him as Prefect of Ningguo, and urged him to report to court, comforting him with especial warmth.

sentences.zh: 魏王出镇，移守婺州。

translations.literal: When Prince Wei went to his fief, Cong was moved to guard Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei went out to his fief, Cong was transferred to guard Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年春，复奉祠，亟告老。

translations.literal: The next spring he received a sinecure again and urgently petitioned to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring he received a sinecure post again and urgently petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 十月卒，年六十，积阶至右中奉大夫，封长兴县男。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth month at the age of sixty; accumulated rank to Right Grand Master for Direct Administration, ennobled as Baron of Changxing County.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month at the age of sixty, having risen to Right Grand Master for Direct Administration and been ennobled as Baron of Changxing County.

sentences.zh: 刘章，字文孺，衢州龙游人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhang, courtesy name Wenru, was a native of Longyou in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang, courtesy name Wenru, was a native of Longyou in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 少警异，日诵数千言，通《小戴礼》，四冠乡举。

translations.literal: From youth he was remarkably bright, recited thousands of characters daily, mastered the Little Dai Rites, and topped the provincial examinations four times.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was unusually quick, recited thousands of characters each day, mastered the Rites of Dai the Younger, and topped the provincial examinations four times.

sentences.zh: 绍兴十五年廷对，考官定其级在三，迨进御，上擢为第一，授镇江军签判。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shaoxing, at the palace examination, the examiners ranked him third; when his paper was presented to the emperor, the emperor raised him to first place and appointed him signatory judge of the Zhenjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination in 1145, the examiners placed him third, but when his answer was read before the emperor, the throne promoted him to first rank and appointed him signatory judge of the Zhenjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 是冬，入省为正字。

translations.literal: That winter, he entered the Secretariat as a collator.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he entered the Secretariat as a collator.

sentences.zh: 明年，迁秘书郎兼 普安、恩平两王府教授，迁著作佐郎。

translations.literal: The next year, he was transferred to secretary gentleman and concurrently served as instructor to the Princes of Pu'an and Enping; he was then transferred to assistant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made secretary gentleman and concurrently instructor to the Princes of Pu'an and Enping, and was later promoted to assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 事王邸四岁，尽忠诚，专以经谊文学启迪掖导，受知孝宗自此始。

translations.literal: He served the princely household for four years with complete loyalty, devoting himself to guiding and instructing through the classics, moral principle, and literary learning; from this time he began to win the esteem of Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: For four years in the princely household he served with unwavering loyalty, teaching through the classics and literature, and from that time Emperor Xiaozong came to know and trust him.

sentences.zh: 秦桧当国，嗛不附已，风言者媒蘖其罪，出倅筠州。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui held power, he resented that Zhang had not attached himself to him; rumor-mongers fabricated charges against him, and he was sent out as deputy prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui dominated the court, he resented Zhang's refusal to join his faction; slanderers invented charges against him, and Zhang was demoted to deputy prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 桧死， 召为司封员外郎、检详枢密院文字兼玉牒检讨官。

translations.literal: After Qin Hui died, Zhang was recalled as outer-section vice director of the Department of State Affairs and reviewer of documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, concurrently serving as reviser of the imperial genealogy.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui's death he was recalled as vice director in the Department of State Affairs, reviewer of documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and reviser of the imperial genealogy.

sentences.zh: 擢秘书少监、起居郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and recorder of the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and imperial recorder.

sentences.zh: 使金还，除权工部侍郎，俄兼吏部、兼侍讲。

translations.literal: On returning from an embassy to Jin, he was appointed acting vice minister of Works; soon afterward he also held the Ministry of Personnel and served as lecturer to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from an embassy to Jin, he was made acting vice minister of Works and soon added concurrent duties in the Ministry of Personnel and as imperial lecturer.

sentences.zh: 郊祀毕，侍从，上《庆成诗》。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was completed, he attended the emperor and submitted a 'Poem on the Completion of the Sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he attended the emperor and presented a poem celebrating its completion.

sentences.zh: 初，章在秘省，尝议郊庙礼文，当置局讨论，诏行其说。

translations.literal: Earlier, while Zhang was in the Secretariat, he had proposed that the ritual texts for the suburban and temple sacrifices should be discussed by a special bureau; an edict ordered his proposal carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while serving in the Secretariat, Zhang had argued that ritual texts for the suburban and temple sacrifices should be studied by a special bureau, and the court adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 正迁吏部，御史论章使胥长买绢，高宗愕然曰：“刘章必无是事。

translations.literal: Just as he was being transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, a censor impeached Zhang for having a clerk chief purchase silk on his behalf. Emperor Gaozong was startled and said, 'Liu Zhang surely would never do such a thing.'
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was being transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, a censor accused him of having a chief clerk buy silk on his behalf. Emperor Gaozong was astonished and said, 'Liu Zhang would never do such a thing.'

sentences.zh: ”御史执不已，罢提举崇道观，举朝嗟 郁。

translations.literal: The censor persisted without cease, and Zhang was dismissed to serve as superintendent of the Chongdao Temple; the whole court sighed in distress.
translations.idiomatic: The censor would not let the matter drop, and Zhang was removed to serve as superintendent of the Chongdao Temple, to the grief and indignation of the entire court.

sentences.zh: 起居郎王佐讼其冤，亦坐绌。

translations.literal: Wang Zuo, recorder of the emperor's movements, pleaded Zhang's innocence and was also demoted for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo, the imperial recorder, appealed on Zhang's behalf and was demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 起知信州，未久，复请祠。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Xinzhou; before long he again requested a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Xinzhou, but before long he again asked to be granted a sinecure at a temple.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禅，念旧学，命知漳州，为谏议大夫王大宝所格。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, remembering his former teacher, he ordered Zhang appointed prefect of Zhangzhou, but Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Wang Dabao blocked the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, he remembered his old tutor and ordered Zhang appointed prefect of Zhangzhou, but Remonstrance Adviser Wang Dabao blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 寻除秘阁修撰、敷文阁待制，召提举佑神观兼 侍读，遂拜礼部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed compiler at the Secret Repository and awaiting orders at the Fuwen Pavilion; he was summoned to serve as superintendent of the Youshen Temple and concurrently as imperial reader, and was then appointed vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made compiler at the Secret Repository and awaiting orders at the Fuwen Pavilion, then summoned to superintend the Youshen Temple while serving as imperial reader, and finally appointed vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 奏禁遏淫祀，仍于《三朝史》中删去《道释》、《符瑞志》，大略以为非《春秋》法。

translations.literal: He memorialized to suppress improper cults, and also proposed deleting from the History of Three Reigns the sections on Daoism and Buddhism and on portents and omens, broadly holding that such material was not in the spirit of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to suppress illicit cult worship and to remove from the History of Three Reigns the sections on Daoism, Buddhism, and portents, arguing in general that such material did not accord with the standards of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 朝廷议经略中原，调诸郡兵，民颇扰。

translations.literal: When the court debated plans to recover the Central Plains, it mobilized troops from the various prefectures, and the people were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated recovering the Central Plains and mobilized troops from the prefectures, the people were greatly troubled.

sentences.zh: 少 卿赵彦端指言非是。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhao Yanduan pointed out that this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhao Yanduan openly argued that the policy was mistaken.

sentences.zh: 或谮彦端曰：“陛下究心大举，凡所图回，但资赵彦端一笑尔。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Yanduan, saying, 'Your Majesty is wholly devoted to this great campaign; every plan you turn over exists only to furnish Zhao Yanduan a laugh.'
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Yanduan, saying, 'Your Majesty is wholly committed to this great campaign, yet every plan you make exists only to amuse Zhao Yanduan.'

sentences.zh: ”颜端惧不测。

translations.literal: Yanduan feared some unforeseen disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Yanduan feared he might suffer some unforeseen punishment.

sentences.zh: 上因夜对问章曰：“闻卿监中有笑朕者。

translations.literal: The emperor, during a night audience, asked Zhang, 'I hear there are people in your office who laugh at me.'
translations.idiomatic: During a night audience the emperor asked Zhang, 'I hear there are people in your office who laugh at me.'

sentences.zh: ”章不知状，从容对 曰：“圣主所为，人焉敢笑，若议论不同或有之。

translations.literal: Zhang, not knowing the details, replied calmly, 'What a sage ruler does—who would dare laugh? If there are differences of opinion, that may well be so.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, unaware of the circumstances, replied calmly, 'Who would dare laugh at what a sage ruler does? Differences of opinion may exist, but mockery would not.'

sentences.zh: ”上意颇解。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was largely eased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger largely subsided.

sentences.zh: 彦端获免，人称章长者。

translations.literal: Yanduan escaped punishment, and people praised Zhang as a man of magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Yanduan was spared, and people praised Zhang as a man of generous character.

sentences.zh: 诏询唐太宗所问魏征德仁功利优劣，章上疏谆复，且言：“太宗问徵在贞观 十六年，陛下宅天命十载于兹，原益加意，将越商、周绍唐、虞矣，太宗非难到也。

translations.literal: An edict asked about the question Emperor Taizong of Tang had put to Wei Zheng concerning the relative merits of virtue, benevolence, utility, and profit. Zhang submitted a lengthy, earnest memorial and said, 'Taizong questioned Wei Zheng in the sixteenth year of Zhenguan; Your Majesty has held the Mandate of Heaven for ten years now. I hope you will give the matter even greater attention—you will surpass the Shang and Zhou and inherit from Tang and Yu; reaching Taizong's level is not difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: The court asked about Emperor Taizong's question to Wei Zheng on the relative merits of virtue, benevolence, utility, and profit. Zhang submitted a long, earnest memorial, saying, 'Taizong put that question to Wei Zheng in 642; Your Majesty has held the Mandate of Heaven for ten years now. I hope you will devote even greater attention to such matters—you may surpass the Shang and Zhou and inherit the legacy of Tang and Yu; matching Taizong is not beyond reach.'

sentences.zh: ”进权礼部尚书兼给事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting minister of Rites and concurrently appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting minister of Rites and concurrently appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 对选德殿，问章：“今年几而容貌未衰，颇尝学道 否？

translations.literal: At an audience in the Xuande Hall, the emperor asked Zhang, 'How old are you this year, that your appearance has not yet declined? Have you perhaps studied the Way?'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience in the Xuande Hall, the emperor asked Zhang, 'How old are you this year, that you still look so vigorous? Have you studied the Way?'

sentences.zh: ”章拱对曰：“臣书生无他长，惟菲俭自度。

translations.literal: Zhang bowed and replied, 'Your servant is a scholar with no other special talent; I have only measured myself by frugality and restraint.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang bowed and replied, 'I am only a scholar with no special gifts; I have simply lived by frugality and restraint.'

sentences.zh: 晏婴一狐裘三十年不易，人以为难，臣以为易。

translations.literal: Yan Ying wore one fox-fur robe for thirty years without changing it; others thought that difficult, but I think it easy.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying wore the same fox-fur robe for thirty years without replacing it; others find that hard, but I find it easy.'

sentences.zh: ”上嘉叹久之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed over this for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly and sighed with admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 亲洒宸翰以赐，俾安职。

translations.literal: He personally wrote in the imperial hand to bestow it upon him and ordered him to resume his duties in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote in his own hand to bestow the gift and told Zhang to resume his duties at ease.

sentences.zh: 章力告归，以显谟阁学士 食祠禄。

translations.literal: Zhang repeatedly requested to retire and was granted the title of academician of the Xianmo Pavilion with temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang repeatedly asked to retire and was granted the title of academician of the Xianmo Pavilion with a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年，子之衡由御史、检法出守广德军，当陛辞，对便殿，问：“卿父学士安否？

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi, Zhang's son Zhihéng, having served as censor and legal inspector, went out to govern Guangde Army; when he took leave at court and had an audience in the side hall, the emperor asked, 'Is your father the academician well?'
translations.idiomatic: In 1174, Zhang's son Zhihéng, who had served as censor and legal inspector, was sent to govern Guangde Army; at his farewell audience in the side hall, the emperor asked, 'Is your father the academician well?'

sentences.zh: ”抚劳再三，临退复谓曰：“卿归侍，为朕致此意。

translations.literal: He comforted and encouraged him again and again, and as he was about to withdraw said again, 'When you return home to attend him, convey this message for me.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him repeatedly, and as he was leaving said again, 'When you return home to attend your father, convey this message for me.'

sentences.zh: ” 旋遣阁门祗候苏曦至家宣问，拜端明殿学士，赐银绢四百匹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he sent the Gate Attendant Su Xi to Zhang's home with an imperial inquiry; Zhang was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and granted four hundred bolts of silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon sent Gate Attendant Su Xi to Zhang's home with an imperial message of inquiry, appointed him academician of the Duanming Hall, and granted him four hundred bolts of silver and silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，上表告老，以资政殿学士致仕，卒，年八十，赠光禄大夫，谥曰靖文。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement, was granted retirement as academician of the Zizheng Hall, and died at the age of eighty; he was posthumously awarded the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the posthumous name Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he memorialized to retire, was granted retirement as academician of the Zizheng Hall, and died at eighty; he was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the posthumous name Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 章容状魁硕，以周密自 守，出入两朝，被顾遇，未尝泄禁中一语。

translations.literal: Zhang was tall and imposing in appearance; he guarded himself with meticulous care. Serving through two reigns and enjoying imperial favor, he never once revealed a single word from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was tall and imposing in bearing and guarded himself with meticulous care. Serving through two reigns and enjoying imperial favor, he never once disclosed a word spoken within the palace.

sentences.zh: 沈作宾

translations.literal: Shen Zuobin
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuobin

sentences.zh: 沈作宾，字宾王，世为吴兴归安人。

translations.literal: Shen Zuobin, courtesy name Binwang, was a native of Gui'an in Wuxing for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zuobin, courtesy name Binwang, came from a family long established in Gui'an, Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 以父任入仕，监饶州永平监，冶铸坚致，又承诏造雁翎刀，称上意，连 进两资。

translations.literal: Entering office through his father's privilege, he supervised the Yongping Foundry in Raozhou; the castings were solid and fine, and when he was also ordered to manufacture goose-quill blades, they pleased the emperor, earning him two consecutive step promotions in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Entering office through his father's privilege, he supervised the Yongping Foundry in Raozhou, where his castings were exceptionally solid; when he was also ordered to manufacture goose-quill blades that pleased the emperor, he received two consecutive step promotions.

sentences.zh: 中刑法科，历江西提刑司检法官，入为大理评事。

translations.literal: He passed the law examination, served as reviewing legal officer in the Jiangxi Circuit Intendant's office for punishments, and entered the capital as an evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the law examination, served as reviewing legal officer under the Jiangxi judicial intendant, and entered the capital as an evaluator at the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 改秩，通判绍兴府。

translations.literal: After a change of rank, he was appointed vice prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a change of rank, he was appointed vice prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帅守丘崇遇僚吏刚严，作宾从容裨赞，每济以宽。

translations.literal: The prefect Qiu Chong was stern and severe with his staff; Zuobin assisted him calmly and always tempered his rigor with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Qiu Chong was stern with his staff; Zuobin assisted him calmly and always softened his severity with leniency.

sentences.zh: 秩满，知台州，首访民疾苦，弛盐 禁，宽租期，均徭役，更酒政，决滞狱，五十日间尽除前政之不便民者，邦人胥悦；

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed prefect of Taizhou; he first inquired into the people's hardships, relaxed the salt monopoly, extended rent deadlines, equalized corvée labor, reformed wine administration, and cleared backlogged cases; within fifty days he removed every inconvenience left by the previous administration, and the people were all delighted;
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he became prefect of Taizhou; he first inquired into the people's hardships, relaxed the salt monopoly, extended rent deadlines, equalized corvée labor, reformed wine administration, and cleared backlogged cases; within fifty days he removed every policy of the previous administration that had harmed the people, and the whole prefecture rejoiced;

sentences.zh: 而前守嫉其胜己，巧媒蘖之，罢去。

translations.literal: But the former prefect, jealous that he outshone him, cleverly fabricated charges against him, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: But the former prefect, jealous that Zuobin outshone him, cleverly fabricated charges against him, and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 民请于朝，借留不遂，为立“留贤碑”。

translations.literal: The people petitioned the court to retain him, but without success; they erected a stele called 'Stele to Retain the Worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned the court to keep him, but without success; they erected a stele called 'Stele to Retain the Worthy.'

sentences.zh: 除 大理正，亲嫌，改太府丞，迁刑部郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review; because of a relative in the office, he was transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and then promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review; because of a relative in the office, he was transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and then promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 庆元初，历官至淮南转运判官，以治办闻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qingyuan era he rose through the ranks to transport commissioner of Huainan East Circuit and was known for effective administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingyuan era he rose through the ranks to transport commissioner of Huainan East Circuit and was known for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 直华文阁，因其任。

translations.literal: He was granted direct access to the Huawen Pavilion in connection with that office.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted direct access to the Huawen Pavilion in connection with that office.

sentences.zh: 擢太府少卿，总领淮东军马钱粮，继升为卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, put in charge of military funds and grain for Huainan East, and later promoted to full director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, put in charge of military funds and grain for Huainan East, and later promoted to full director.

sentences.zh: 寻 除直龙图阁，帅浙东，知绍兴府。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed directly to the Longtu Pavilion, given command of Zhedong Circuit, and appointed prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed directly to the Longtu Pavilion, given command of Zhedong Circuit, and appointed prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 入对，奏：“徽州、南康军月桩不如期，朝廷科降额，比年曰‘权免一次’，来年督促如初，适足启吏奸、重民害，乞明诏示。

translations.literal: At an audience he memorialized, 'When Huizhou and Nankang Circuit fail to meet their monthly quota assessments on time, the court reduces their quotas; in recent years this has been called a one-time temporary exemption, but the next year collection is enforced as before. This only encourages official corruption and increases harm to the people. I beg that an explicit edict be issued to make this clear.'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he memorialized, 'When Huizhou and Nankang Circuit fail to meet their monthly quota assessments on time, the court reduces their quotas; in recent years this has been called a one-time temporary exemption, but the next year collection is enforced as before. This only encourages official corruption and increases harm to the people. I beg that an explicit edict be issued to make this clear.'

sentences.zh: 又 楚州武锋一军已招三千五百餘人，朝廷初欲减戍，数年未就纪律：一，主将望轻；

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Wufeng Army of Chuzhou has already recruited more than thirty-five hundred men; the court initially wished to reduce the garrison, but for several years discipline has not been established: first, the commanding general lacks sufficient standing;
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the Wufeng Army of Chuzhou has already recruited more than thirty-five hundred men; the court initially wished to reduce the garrison, but for several years discipline has not been established: first, the commanding general lacks sufficient standing;

sentences.zh: 二，郡守节制不为礼；

translations.literal: second, the prefect does not treat him with the proper respect due to military command;
translations.idiomatic: second, the prefect does not treat him with the proper respect due to military command;

sentences.zh: 三，训练不尽其能。

translations.literal: third, training has not fully developed their capabilities.
translations.idiomatic: third, training has not fully developed their capabilities.

sentences.zh: 愿令本州少假借，责之练习，期以岁 月，考绩用成否，上于朝而黜陟之。

translations.literal: I ask that the prefect be allowed a little discretion, that they be required to drill, that a deadline of months be set, and that success or failure be assessed and reported to the court for promotion or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the prefect be allowed a little discretion, that they be required to drill, that a deadline of months be set, and that success or failure be assessed and reported to the court for promotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: ”上嘉纳。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 韩侂胄方用事，族有居越者，私酿公行，作宾逮捕置于狱，而窜其奴。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou was then in power; a clansman of his living in Yue privately brewed liquor openly, and Zuobin arrested him and placed him in prison, banishing his servants.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was then in power; a clansman of his living in Yue privately brewed liquor openly, and Zuobin arrested him and placed him in prison, banishing his servants.

sentences.zh: 又论绍兴府和买事，语在《食货志》。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on the hemai purchases in Shaoxing Prefecture; the account is given in the Treatise on Food and Money.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on the hemai purchases in Shaoxing Prefecture; the account is given in the Treatise on Food and Money.

sentences.zh: 除两浙转运副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhe Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhe Circuits.

sentences.zh: 入对，奏：“欑宫一司，岁拔经、总制钱为缗率四万有奇，丹雘未弊，加之涂饰，墙壁具存，从而创易，妄费固不足计，亡谓惊黩，非所以妥神灵、彰圣孝。

translations.literal: At an audience he memorialized, 'The office for the temporary imperial tomb consumes more than forty thousand strings of cash each year drawn from regular and aggregate funds; though the cinnabar lacquer is not yet damaged, more is added for repainting; though the walls remain intact, they are torn down and rebuilt. The waste is not worth calculating, but worse, it is wantonly disturbing and irreverent—not the way to put the spirits at rest or display imperial filial piety.'
translations.idiomatic: At an audience he memorialized, 'The office for the temporary imperial tomb consumes more than forty thousand strings of cash each year drawn from regular and aggregate funds; though the cinnabar lacquer is not yet damaged, more is added for repainting; though the walls remain intact, they are torn down and rebuilt. The waste is not worth calculating, but worse, it is wantonly disturbing and irreverent—not the way to put the spirits at rest or display imperial filial piety.'

sentences.zh: 今后有合营缮，闻于朝，下守臣稽核，画旨而后兴役。

translations.literal: Hereafter, whenever repairs are needed, the matter should be reported to the court, the local official should verify it, and work should begin only after an imperial directive is issued.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, whenever repairs are needed, the matter should be reported to the court, the local official should verify it, and work should begin only after an imperial directive is issued.

sentences.zh: ”上首肯再三，而修奉者不乐也。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent again and again, but those in charge of maintenance were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent again and again, but those in charge of maintenance were displeased.

sentences.zh: 除权工部侍郎，继兼户部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting vice minister of Works and soon also held the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting vice minister of Works and soon also held the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 奏请修绍兴三十一年以前故事，复敕令所删修官五员以待选人有才者，又乞申严保伍法。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting restoration of precedents from before the thirty-first year of Shaoxing, reinstatement of five revisers at the Statutes Office to await talented candidates, and also asked that the baowu system be strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized requesting restoration of precedents from before 1161, reinstatement of five revisers at the Statutes Office to await talented candidates, and also asked that the baowu system be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 以言者罢归，起知镇江府，除集英殿修 撰，改知宁国府，除宝谟阁待制，知潭州，除户部侍郎兼详定敕令官。

translations.literal: Because of critics he was dismissed and sent home; he was then recalled to govern Zhenjiang Prefecture, appointed compiler at the Jiying Hall, transferred to govern Ningguo Prefecture, appointed awaiting orders at the Baomo Pavilion, appointed prefect of Tanzhou, and appointed vice minister of Revenue concurrently as commissioner for the detailed revision of statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Because of critics he was dismissed and sent home; he was then recalled to govern Zhenjiang Prefecture, appointed compiler at the Jiying Hall, transferred to govern Ningguo Prefecture, appointed awaiting orders at the Baomo Pavilion, appointed prefect of Tanzhou, and appointed vice minister of Revenue concurrently as commissioner for the detailed revision of statutes.

sentences.zh: 奏湖北当储粟，湖南当增兵。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Hubei should store grain and Hunan should increase troops.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Hubei should store grain and Hunan should increase troops.

sentences.zh: 未几，除龙图阁待制，知平江府，请得节制许浦水军，诏可。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed awaiting orders at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; he requested command over the naval forces at Xupu, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed awaiting orders at the Longtu Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; he requested command over the naval forces at Xupu, and the edict approved.

sentences.zh: 郡 有使臣，故海盗也，作宾使招诱其党，既至，慰勉之，锡衣物，又得强勇者几千人，置将以统之，号曰“义士”；

translations.literal: In the prefecture there was an envoy who had formerly been a pirate; Zuobin sent men to entice his followers, and once they arrived he comforted and encouraged them, bestowed clothing, and also obtained several thousand strong and brave men whom he placed under commanders, calling them 'Righteous Warriors';
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture there was an envoy who had formerly been a pirate; Zuobin sent men to entice his followers, and once they arrived he comforted and encouraged them, bestowed clothing, and also obtained several thousand strong and brave men whom he placed under commanders, calling them 'Righteous Warriors';

sentences.zh: 复募郡城内外恶少亦几千人，号曰“壮士”。

translations.literal: He also recruited several thousand unruly youths inside and outside the prefectural city, calling them 'Bold Warriors.'
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited several thousand unruly youths inside and outside the prefectural city, calling them 'Bold Warriors.'

sentences.zh: 衣粮 器械皆视官军，而轻捷善斗过之，于是海道不警，市井无哗。

translations.literal: Their clothing, rations, and weapons were all on a par with regular troops, yet they were more agile and better in combat; thereafter the sea routes were secure and the markets quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Their clothing, rations, and weapons were all on a par with regular troops, yet they were more agile and better in combat; thereafter the sea routes were secure and the markets quiet.

sentences.zh: 寻命参赞督府，兼权镇江府。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to assist the supervisory headquarters and concurrently act as prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to assist the supervisory headquarters and concurrently act as prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 请留戍兵千人，又欲以江、闽新军二千人易旧军千人，备不虞。

translations.literal: He requested that a thousand garrison troops be retained, and also wished to exchange a thousand old troops for two thousand new troops from Jiang and Min as a precaution against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that a thousand garrison troops be retained, and also wished to exchange a thousand old troops for two thousand new troops from Jiang and Min as a precaution against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 朝廷难 之，遂请祠。

translations.literal: The court found this difficult to accept, and he thereupon requested a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court found this difficult to accept, and he thereupon requested a temple appointment.

sentences.zh: 言者继及之，复召为户部侍郎。

translations.literal: Criticism continued, and he was again recalled as vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Criticism continued, and he was again recalled as vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 军兴之餘，国力殚耗，见存金谷，仅支旬日。

translations.literal: In the aftermath of the military campaign, national strength was exhausted; the treasury's remaining gold and grain would barely last ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the military campaign, national strength was exhausted; the treasury's remaining gold and grain would barely last ten days.

sentences.zh: 作宾考逋负，柅吏奸，阅三月即有半年之储。

translations.literal: Zuobin investigated arrears and checked official corruption; within three months there was a six-month reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Zuobin investigated arrears and checked official corruption; within three months there was a six-month reserve.

sentences.zh: 充馆伴使，兼权工部尚书。

translations.literal: He served as host for the embassy and concurrently acted as minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served as host for the embassy and concurrently acted as minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 会临安阙知府事，时相欲奏用作宾，力辞。

translations.literal: When Lin'an lacked a prefect, the chief councilor wished to recommend Zuobin, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin'an lacked a prefect, the chief councilor wished to recommend Zuobin, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 除权户部尚书，以母忧解，服阕，授显谟阁直学士、知建宁府。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting minister of Revenue; he resigned on account of mourning for his mother, and after the mourning period was appointed direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting minister of Revenue; he resigned on account of mourning for his mother, and after the mourning period was appointed direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 入觐，乞申严诡户之禁。

translations.literal: On presenting himself at court he requested strict enforcement of the prohibition on fraudulent household registration.
translations.idiomatic: On presenting himself at court he requested strict enforcement of the prohibition on fraudulent household registration.

sentences.zh: 除宝谟阁学士、江西安抚兼知 隆兴府。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Baomo Pavilion, military commissioner of Jiangxi, and concurrently prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Baomo Pavilion, military commissioner of Jiangxi, and concurrently prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 奏部内南安、南康、龙泉三县，迫近溪峒，三县令尉及近峒之砦曰秀洲，曰北乡，曰莲塘，并永新县之胜乡砦，宜就委帅、宪两司择才辟置，量加赏格。

translations.literal: He memorialized that within his jurisdiction the three counties of Nan'an, Nankang, and Longquan, close to the stream gorges and mountain passes, together with the county magistrates and sheriffs and the nearby stockades called Xiuzhou, Beixiang, and Liantang, as well as the Shengxiang stockade in Yongxin County, should be entrusted to the circuit commander and judicial intendant to select talented men for appointment, with added rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that within his jurisdiction the three counties of Nan'an, Nankang, and Longquan, close to the stream gorges and mountain passes, together with the county magistrates and sheriffs and the nearby stockades called Xiuzhou, Beixiang, and Liantang, as well as the Shengxiang stockade in Yongxin County, should be entrusted to the circuit commander and judicial intendant to select talented men for appointment, with added rewards according to rank.

sentences.zh: 又 乞诏诸道监司分诣州郡，选禁军，精练阅，改刺其懦弱者为厢军。

translations.literal: He also asked that an edict order circuit supervisors to go in person to the prefectures, select troops from the forbidden armies, drill and review them carefully, and reassign the weak to the auxiliary armies.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that an edict order circuit supervisors to go in person to the prefectures, select troops from the forbidden armies, drill and review them carefully, and reassign the weak to the auxiliary armies.

sentences.zh: 在郡撙钱二十餘万缗，僚属请献诸朝，作宾谓平生未尝献羡，以半归帅司犒师，半隶本府。

translations.literal: While in the prefecture he saved more than two hundred thousand strings of cash; his staff asked to present the surplus to the court, but Zuobin said he had never in his life presented surplus revenue; he gave half to the command headquarters to reward the troops and kept half for the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While in the prefecture he saved more than two hundred thousand strings of cash; his staff asked to present the surplus to the court, but Zuobin said he had never in his life presented surplus revenue; he gave half to the command headquarters to reward the troops and kept half for the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 除焕章 阁学士、提举隆兴府玉隆万寿宫，进显谟阁学士致仕，卒于家，赠金紫光禄大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and superintendent of the Yulong Wanshou Temple in Longxing Prefecture, advanced to direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion with retirement, died at home, and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and superintendent of the Yulong Wanshou Temple in Longxing Prefecture, advanced to direct academician of the Xianmo Pavilion with retirement, died at home, and was posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 论曰：李衡进退雍容，几于闻道。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Li Heng advanced and withdrew with dignified ease, nearly attaining the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Li Heng advanced and withdrew with dignified ease, nearly attaining the Way.

sentences.zh: 王自中、家愿奇迈危言，摧折弗 悔，咸有可称。

translations.literal: Wang Zizhong and Jia Yuan were bold and outspoken in perilous words; though broken, they did not repent—all had qualities worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zizhong and Jia Yuan were bold and outspoken in perilous words; though broken, they did not repent—all had qualities worth praising.

sentences.zh: 尝考宋之立国，元气在台谏。

translations.literal: Having examined the founding of Song, its vital spirit lay in the censorial and remonstrance offices.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, when the Song state was founded, its strength lay in the censorial and remonstrance institutions.

sentences.zh: 崇宁、大观而后，奸佞擅权，爵赏冒滥，驯至覆亡。

translations.literal: After the Chongning and Daguan eras, wicked flatterers monopolized power, ranks and rewards were recklessly dispensed, and this led step by step to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chongning and Daguan periods, wicked flatterers seized power, titles and rewards were handed out with reckless abandon, and the dynasty drifted inexorably toward collapse.

sentences.zh: 高、孝重绳纠封驳之司，张纲抑令懬恩，大经劾韩俣、斥董琏，人 人振扬风采，正气稍伸矣。

translations.literal: Gaozong and Xiaozong valued the offices of scrutiny and memorial rejection; Zhang Gang restrained Ling Kuan's favoritism, Dajing impeached Han Yu and rebuked Dong Lian—each man displayed his moral bearing, and righteous spirit was somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong and Xiaozong, the offices charged with scrutiny and blocking improper edicts were again taken seriously. Zhang Gang held back the special favor shown to Ling Kuan; Zhang Dajing impeached the attendant Han Yu and denounced the eunuch Dong Lian. Each in his way revived the censorial spirit, and the moral climate improved somewhat.

sentences.zh: 时则有若洸、濛、淙、章、作宾，班班有善，同传亦宜。

translations.literal: In that age there were men such as Guang, Meng, Cong, Zhang, and Zuobin—each in his station had merit; they too are fit to share this collective biography.
translations.idiomatic: In the same period there were figures such as Cai Guang, Mo Meng, Zhou Cong, Liu Zhang, and Shen Zuobin—each distinguished in his own way, and all deserving to appear in this shared biography.
